title: Homemade Cocktail Bitters
text: homemade cocktail bitters source: the spruce eats ingredients - 1 cup 151-proof grain alcohol - 1 tablespoon quassia bark - 1 teaspoon cardamom seeds - 1 teaspoon coriander seeds - 1 teaspoon dried orange peel, minced - 1/2 teaspoon caraway seeds - 1/2 teaspoon dried gentian root - 2 cups water - 1/3 cup sugar instructions 1. in a 1-pint jar or larger, combine 1 cup 151-proof grain alcohol, 1 tablespoon quassia bark, 1 teaspoon cardamom seeds, 1 teaspoon coriander seeds, 1 teaspoon minced dried orange peel, 1/2 teaspoon caraway seeds, and 1/2 teaspoon dried gentian root. 2. seal the jar, shake, and let the mixture stand in a cool, dark place for 14 days, shaking vigorously once a day. 3. strain the infused alcohol into a clean jar through cheesecloth to remove the botanicals, gathering the cloth into a ball and squeezing to release as much liquid as possible. 4. use a muddler or mortar and pestle to break up the strained botanicals as much as possible. 5. in a medium nonreactive saucepan, add 2 cups water and the botanicals, then bring to a boil. 6. cover and lower the heat, allowing the mixture to simmer for 5 to 7 minutes. 7. pour the mixture without straining into a 1-pint jar or larger, cover, and allow it to sit for 5 days in a cool and dry place, shaking vigorously once a day. 8. strain the infused water through cheesecloth and discard the botanicals. 9. measure the infused alcohol and combine it with an equal amount of aromatic water in a 1-pint jar or larger. 10. in a small saucepan over medium-high heat, add 1/3 cup sugar, stir constantly, and allow the sugar to caramelize until dark brown, about 3 to 4 minutes. 11. add the caramelized sugar to the alcohol and water mixture and let it dissolve within a few minutes. 12. shake the bitters, then strain through cheesecloth to remove any sediment. 13. pour into a bitters bottle or small decanter with a tight-sealing lid and store for up to 12 months unrefrigerated in a cool place.

title: Homemade Marshmallow Fluff
text: homemade marshmallow fluff source: livforcake.com ingredients - 1/3 cup water - 3/4 cup granulated sugar - 3/4 cup corn syrup (or honey) - 3 large egg whites (room temperature) - 1/2 tsp cream of tartar - 1 tsp vanilla extract instructions 1. place water, sugar, and corn syrup in a medium saucepan. stir to combine. 2. insert a candy thermometer into the pot and heat over medium-high. do not stir from this point on as crystals will form. 3. wipe down your mixer bowl, whisk, etc with lemon juice or vinegar to ensure they are completely grease free. 4. place egg whites and cream of tartar in the bowl of a stand mixer. 5. when the sugar syrup reaches about 225°f, start whipping the egg whites to soft peaks. approx 3-4mins. 6. when the whites are ready, the sugar syrup should be at 240°f. remove from the heat, turn mixer to medium and very slowly and carefully pour the sugar syrup into the whites in a thin, steady stream. 7. once all of the syrup is in, set mixer to medium/high and continue whipping. the whites will deflate at first, but they will thicken and fluff up. 8. continue to whip for 7-8 minutes, or until the mixture is thick and fluffy. 9. add in vanilla and whip until the fluff has cooled completely. 10. use right away as a frosting or filling or transfer into an airtight container and store for up to 2 weeks at room temperature.

title: Homemade Oatmeal Cream Pies
text: homemade oatmeal cream pies source: mybakingaddiction.com ingredients - 1 cup unsalted butter (softened) - 3/4 cup firmly packed light brown sugar - 1/2 cup granulated sugar - 2 large eggs - 1 teaspoon pure vanilla extract - 1 1/2 cups all-purpose flour - 1 teaspoon baking soda - 1 teaspoon ground cinnamon - 1/2 teaspoon salt - 3 cups quick or old fashioned oats - 3/4 cup unsalted butter (softened) - 2 1/2 cups confectioners' sugar (sifted) - 1 teaspoon pure vanilla extract - 1 tablespoon milk or half and half instructions 1. preheat oven to 350°f. line cookie sheets with parchment paper. 2. in the bowl of a stand mixer fitted with the paddle attachment, or in a large bowl with an electric mixer, cream together butter and sugars until light and fluffy, about 3 minutes. add in eggs and vanilla and mix until combined. 3. in a medium bowl, whisk together the flour, baking soda, cinnamon and salt. slowly add the flour mixture to the wet ingredients, mixing until just combined. add in oats and mix until incorporated. 4. to make large cookies, use a large cookie scoop (about 3 tablespoons) to drop dough onto prepared cookie sheets. bake in preheated oven for 13-15 minutes or until golden brown. to make small cookies, use a medium cookie scoop (about 1.5 tablespoons) of dough per cookie and bake for 10-12 minutes. 5. allow cookies to sit on cookie sheets for about 5 minutes before removing them to a wire rack to cool completely. once cookies have cooled completely, prepare the cream filling. 6. in the bowl of a stand mixer fitted with the paddle attachment or in a large bowl with an electric hand mixer, beat butter on medium-high speed for about 5 minutes. this process will lighten the color of the butter and ensure you buttercream in extra fluffy. 7. turn the speed down to low and gradually add in the powdered sugar. continue mixing on low speed until the powdered sugar is completely incorporated. add in vanilla extract and milk and mix until combined. 8. turn mixer back up to medium-high speed and beat the mixture for an additional 3-5 minutes. if needed, add in a little more milk or half-and-half 1 teaspoon at a time until you reach the consistency you desire. 9. to assemble the cookies, pipe or spread the cream filling on the flat side of half of the cookies and put the remaining cookies on top.

title: Homemade Phyllo (or Filo) Dough
text: homemade phyllo (or filo) dough source: allrecipes.com ingredients - 2 cups all-purpose flour, plus more for kneading - 5 teaspoons olive oil - 1/2 teaspoon fine salt - 3/4 cup warm water (110 degrees f / 43 degrees c) - 2 teaspoons white wine vinegar - 1/2 cup cornstarch - 2 tablespoons all-purpose flour instructions 1. place 2 cups flour in a mixing bowl and make a well in the center, then drizzle in olive oil and add salt. 2. pour in warm water and white wine vinegar, then mix until dough just comes together and pulls away from the sides of the bowl, about 1 to 2 minutes. 3. transfer dough to a lightly floured work surface and knead until smooth, using just enough flour to keep it from sticking, for 2 or 3 minutes, then continue to knead until dough is supple and elastic for about 5 more minutes. 4. wrap dough ball in plastic wrap and let rest at room temperature for 1 to 2 hours. 5. use a kitchen scale to divide dough into twenty 25-gram portions and roll each portion into a ball, then place on a plate and cover with plastic wrap to prevent drying out while working in batches of 5. 6. mix cornstarch and 2 tablespoons flour together in a bowl, then dust a work surface and the first dough ball with the cornstarch mixture. 7. flatten and roll out into a circle about 5 inches in diameter, dust again with cornstarch mixture, then roll out 4 more dough balls to about the same diameter and stack them on the first one, dusting each layer with more cornstarch mixture to keep them from sticking together. 8. roll out the 5-circle stack to a larger circle about double in size, turning as you go to maintain a round shape, then separate each layer and lay out the circles, reapplying more cornstarch mixture where needed and restacking them. 9. roll again until the 5-layer stack is paper-thin, about 10 to 12 inches in diameter, then place on a sheet of parchment paper, top with another piece of parchment, gently roll up the dough, wrap it in plastic wrap, and refrigerate. 10. repeat with the remaining 15 balls of dough in batches of 5.

title: Homemade Pierogi
text: homemade pierogi ingredients - 2 cups (241g) king arthur unbleached all-purpose flour - 1/2 teaspoon salt - 1 large egg - 1/2 cup (113g) sour cream - 4 tablespoons (57g) butter, room temperature - 1 cup (227g) warm mashed potatoes - 1 cup (113g) sharp cheddar cheese, shredded - 4 tablespoons (57g) butter, cold - 2 large (156g) shallots, diced, or one medium (156g) onion, sliced instructions 1. mix together the flour and salt. 2. add the egg to the flour and combine. 3. work in the sour cream and soft butter until the dough comes together in a slightly rough, slightly sticky ball. 4. using just your fingertips, knead and fold the dough without adding additional flour until the dough becomes less sticky but still quite moist. 5. wrap the dough well in plastic wrap and refrigerate for 30 to 60 minutes, or up to 48 hours. 6. combine the warm mashed potato and cheese, stirring and mashing until the cheese is melted and the filling is cool to the touch, then taste and adjust the seasonings with salt and pepper. 7. roll half the dough 1/8" thick and use a 2" round cutter to cut circles of dough, then repeat with the other half of the dough. 8. place 1 1/2 teaspoons of filling on each round of dough. 9. gently fold the dough over, forming a pocket around the filling, then pinch the edges of the pierogi to seal and seal again with the tines of a fork. 10. cook the pierogi in a large stockpot of boiling salted water, cooking about 10 pierogi at a time so they have room to float without sticking, until they float. 11. sauté the shallots or onion in the butter in a large skillet until the onion begins to brown. 12. add the drained pierogi and cook until browned and crisped. 13. serve hot with additional sour cream, applesauce, or other condiments.

title: Homemade Pomegranate Liqueur
text: homemade pomegranate liqueur source: instructables ingredients - roughly six pomegranates, depending on their size - peel of 1 lemon (meyer preferred) - 1 cinnamon stick - 3 cups vodka - 1 1/2 cups white sugar - 3/4 cup water instructions 1. cut the pomegranate in half vertically and fill a large bowl with water. 2. turn the pomegranate half seed-side down and push on the center with your thumbs to turn the half inside-out, working under water to minimize juice spraying. 3. allow the membrane, flesh, and pith to float to the top while seeds fall to the bottom, then rinse and agitate to free any extra membrane. 4. place a fine mesh metal strainer in a bowl and press pomegranate seed pods down against the strainer with a spoon to crush the pods and extract the juice, reserving both seeds and juice. 5. using a vegetable peeler or paring knife, carefully peel the lemon while avoiding the white pith to preserve the oils in the peel. 6. sterilize a large glass jar in boiling water or a dishwasher rinse cycle, then add the pomegranate juice and seeds, lemon peel, and cinnamon stick. 7. pour in the vodka, wipe the rim clean, and seal the jar. 8. store the jar in a cool, dark location and agitate daily with a good swirl for two to three weeks. 9. carefully strain the liquid through several layers of moistened cheesecloth and gently wring to extract all liquid, then discard the rind, pulp, and spices. 10. return the strained liquid to the jar. 11. gently heat the sugar and water on medium-low to create a simple syrup, stirring only until the sugar is dissolved, then allow it to cool completely. 12. add the cooled simple syrup to the jar with the strained liquid. 13. store the jar in a cool, dark, and dry location, agitating every few days, and allow to age for at least three more weeks, ideally four to five weeks. 14. sterilize glass bottles, a funnel, and any transfer utensils in a boiling water bath or dishwasher sterilizing rinse. 15. carefully scoop the liqueur into a glass measuring cup, avoiding any sediment at the bottom. 16. pour the liqueur into sterilized bottles through a funnel, wipe the lids, and seal quickly. 17. serve chilled straight up, mix one-to-one with vodka for a pomegranate martini, or add an ounce to champagne for a festive drink.

title: Sourdough Croissants
text: sourdough croissants source: aberlehome.com ingredients - 115g active sourdough starter, 100% hydration - 36g sugar - 10g kosher salt - 29g (2 tablespoons) unsalted butter, melted - 240g whole milk, cold - 423g unbleached all-purpose flour - 227g (1 cup) 82% fat (european-style) unsalted butter, cold - 8g (1 tablespoon) unbleached all-purpose flour - 1 egg - 15g (1 tablespoon) whole milk instructions 1. feed starter several hours before mixing dough and allow it to peak 2. sourdough croissant dough: 3. 1 4. day 1: mix the dough ingredients until a shaggy dough forms 5. remove dough to a clean countertop and knead for a few minutes until a smooth dough forms 6. form dough into a ball. 7. 2 8. transfer dough to a large bowl and cover 9. leave in a warm place (75°-78°f) to ferment for 4 hours, or until it has nearly doubled in size. 10. 3 11. cover and refrigerate dough overnight 12. butter block: 13. 1 14. day 2: place cold butter on a sheet of parchment paper and sprinkle with the flour 15. fold the ends of the parchment loosely to cover the butter and begin pounding the butter with a rolling pin until it begins to flatten. (update: i find it's easier to measure and fold the parchment before placing the butter inside.) 16. 2 17. use a measuring tape to form the parchment paper into a 6x8-inch rectangle pouch over the butter 18. flip the pouch over to keep the edges closed 19. then use a rolling pin and your fingers to evenly press the butter into the pouch to make a butter block 20. chill if butter has begun to melt and looks greasy on the edges 21. if butter is still cold but very pliable when you bend the package, it is ready for the next step 22. lock in butter block: 23. 1 24. remove dough from fridge and turn it out onto a lightly floured surface 25. use your hands to begin to shape the dough into a rectangle and pinch the corners to shape them 26. roll the dough into a 13x9-inch rectangle. 27. 2 28. unwrap butter block and place in the center of your dough with a short side facing you. 29. 3 30. bring the ends of the dough over the butter so they meet in the middle of the butter block, encasing the butter 31. press every seam to seal so the butter does not escape during rolling 32. brush away any loose flour with a pastry brush 33. first lamination fold (book fold): 34. 1 35. turn the dough so the center seam is parallel to you 36. use your rolling pin to gently pound the dough to lengthen it 37. then roll to a 24x10-inch rectangle 38. try to keep the edges and corners straight, and dust underneath with more flour as needed to prevent sticking. 39. 2 40. fold the short ends of the rectangle inward to meet in the center (update: meeting the edges together off-center is actually better) 41. then fold the new ends together like you're closing a book 42. brush away any loose flour as you go. 43. 3 44. wrap book in plastic wrap and refrigerate for 20 minutes 45. second lamination fold (tri-fold or letter fold): 46. 1 47. place dough on your lightly floured surface again, this time with the fold facing you 48. pound and roll to a 24x10-inch rectangle again. 49. 2 50. fold the short ends of the rectangle in thirds this time, as if you are folding a letter 51. brush away loose flour as you go. 52. 3 53. wrap in plastic again, and chill for 1 hour 54. shaping and baking croissants: 55. 1 56. remove dough from fridge and allow it to rest for 20 minutes or until the butter is pliable again 57. with the folded side facing you, roll to a 18x11.5-inch rectangle 58. use a pizza cutter to trim the edges. 59. 2 60. cut the rectangle into 5 equal rectangles, measuring for accuracy 61. cut each rectangle in half on the diagonal to form 10 triangles. 62. 3 63. set a triangle in front of you with the bottom two corners facing you 64. brush away loose flour 65. gently stretch these corners wider with your fingers and then roll the croissant tight enough that there won't be gaps in the finished pastry. (update: i now make a small cut in the center of the base of each triangle instead of stretching the edges, then roll.) lightly press the tip of the triangle into the croissant to help it adhere to the underneath side 66. repeat for remaining triangles. 67. 4 68. arrange the croissants on 2 parchment-lined half sheet pans, 5 to each pan 69. cover with plastic wrap (not too tightly) and leave at room temperature to proof for several hours (do not exceed 75°f during proofing), or until croissants have doubled in size and wobble like marshmallows when you bump the pan 70. you should begin to see some separation in the layers when proofing is finished 71. meanwhile, preheat your oven to 400°f. 72. 5 73. beat your egg and milk together to make an egg wash 74. use a pastry brush to brush egg wash over each proofed croissant, avoiding the laminated edges. 75. 6 76. bake one pan at a time on the center rack for 15-20 minutes, or until deeply golden brown. (hold second pan in the fridge until you're ready to egg wash and bake if done proofing.) 77. 7 78. place croissants on a cooling rack, and serve or store once they've cooled completely.

title: Honey-Roasted Root Vegetable Salad
text: honey-roasted root vegetable salad source: foodandwine.com ingredients - 1 pound medium beets, with 1 inch of the stem attached - 1 pound carrots, peeled and cut into 1 1/2-inch pieces - 1 pound parsnips, peeled and cut into 1 1/2-inch pieces - 1 pound turnips, peeled and cut into 1 1/2-inch pieces - 3 tablespoons vegetable oil - 3 small white onions (about 3/4 pound), cut into 2-inch wedges - salt and freshly ground pepper - 3 tablespoons honey, warmed - 1 tablespoon chopped sage leaves - 4 ounces fresh goat cheese, at room temperature - 1/4 cup minced fresh herbs, such as chives, tarragon and flat-leaf parsley - 2 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil - 1/4 cup extra-virgin olive oil - 2 tablespoons sherry vinegar - 1 large garlic clove, minced - 1 tablespoon minced herbs, such as chives, tarragon and flat-leaf parsley - salt and freshly ground pepper - 4 cups packed arugula leaves (from two 4-ounce bunches) instructions 1. preheat the oven to 400°. tightly wrap the beets in a double layer of aluminum foil and roast them on the bottom shelf of the oven for 1 1/2 hours, or until they are tender when pierced with the tip of a knife. when the beets are cool enough to handle, peel and cut them into 1-inch pieces. 2. meanwhile, divide the carrots, parsnips and turnips between 2 large rimmed baking sheets. toss the vegetables in each pan with 1 tablespoon of the vegetable oil. arrange the onion wedges on the baking sheets, keeping them intact. brush the onion wedges all over with the remaining 1 tablespoon of vegetable oil. generously season the vegetables with salt and pepper. roast the vegetables for 40 minutes. brush the vegetables with the warm honey and sprinkle with the sage. continue to roast the vegetables for 25 minutes longer, or until they are tender and glazed. loosen the vegetables with a spatula and let them cool to room temperature in the pans. 3. in a small bowl, mix the goat cheese with the herbs and olive oil and season with salt and pepper. 4. in a small bowl, combine the olive oil with the vinegar, garlic and herbs; season with salt and pepper. in a large bowl, toss the arugula with 1 tablespoon of the vinaigrette and arrange on plates. add the roasted vegetables to the bowl and toss with the remaining vinaigrette. top the arugula with the vegetables, dot each plate with small spoonfuls of the herbed goat cheese and serve.

title: Honey Tahini Cookies
text: honey tahini cookies ingredients - ½ cup sesame seeds - 1½ cups almond flour - ½ tsp baking soda - ¼ tsp sea salt - ⅓ cup honey - ⅓ cup tahini - 1 tsp vanilla extract instructions 1. preheat oven to 350°f and line a baking sheet with parchment paper. 2. spread sesame seeds on a shallow plate. 3. in a bowl, whisk together almond flour, baking soda, and sea salt. 4. stir in honey, tahini, and vanilla until a dough forms. 5. roll dough into balls about 1 tablespoon each. 6. roll each ball in the sesame seeds to coat, then place on the prepared baking sheet. 7. flatten each ball slightly with your palm. 8. bake for 8 minutes, until golden around the edges. 9. cool on the pan for 5 minutes before transferring.

title: How I Bake Sourdough Bread
text: how i bake sourdough bread ingredients - 55 gr flour - 55 ml water - sourdough starter - 388 gr flour - 8 g salt - 257 ml water - rice flour instructions 1. at 21:00 in the evening, add 55 gr flour and 55 ml water to your starter jar. 2. put dutch oven in oven to turn on automatically at 06:15 for 1 hour at 220°c. 3. prepare and premix 388 gr flour and 8 g salt in a bowl, keeping 257 ml water ready for the morning. 4. at 07:15, take dough from fridge and banneton, make a cut, and put it into the oven covered. 5. mix the pre-prepared flour, water, starter, and salt to make dough. 6. at 07:35, uncover bread in oven and do a quick knead for about a minute. 7. at 08:05, take out the loaf and give the dough one major stretch and fold before shaping it into a dough ball and placing it back in its bowl. 8. at 13:20, do a quick pre-shape and rest for 10 minutes. 9. at 13:30, shape for the basket, quick roll in rice flour, and place it in a dusted banneton. 10. at 15:00, once dough is expanding and feels springy, pop it into the fridge. 11. wash and dry the bowl and prepare 55 gr flour and 55 ml water.

title: How I Bake Sourdough Bread Every Day in Less Than 30 Minutes
text: how i bake sourdough bread every day in less than 30 minutes source: culinaryexploration.eu ingredients - 55g water (for starter feeding) - 55g strong white bread flour (for starter feeding) - 388g strong white bread flour - 257g water - 8g salt - 98g starter (100% hydrated) - rice flour for dusting instructions 1. feed your sourdough starter at 21:00 with 55g room temperature water and 55g strong white bread flour, using the scrapings left in the jar. 2. the next morning, add 257g water to a bowl and roughly dissolve the 98g starter into it. 3. add 8g salt and stir, then add 388g strong white bread flour and mix with a spoon until all dry flour is incorporated into a rough dough. 4. rest the dough covered in the bowl for 10 minutes, then knead for 1 minute. 5. rest the dough covered at room temperature for 30 minutes. 6. turn the dough out and perform one set of stretch and folds or lamination, then shape into a ball and leave covered at room temperature to bulk ferment for about 6 hours until expanded by 75%. 7. turn the dough out and give it a quick pre-shape, then rest uncovered for 10 minutes. 8. lightly dust the banneton and top of the dough with rice flour, shape the dough simply into a cylinder, and place seam-side up in the banneton. 9. leave the dough out at room temperature uncovered for about 1.5 hours until it feels springy and expanding. 10. pop the dough into the fridge uncovered to ferment overnight. 11. the next morning, preheat your oven to 220°c (430°f) with a baking stone, then score the dough and bake covered with a large pot for the first 20 minutes. 12. uncover and bake for a final 30 minutes without steam until the bread is golden brown.

title: How To Make Butter
text: how to make butter source: thekitchn.com ingredients - 1 pint (2 cups) heavy cream, preferably organic and not ultra-pasteurized - 2 tablespoons plain yogurt (optional) - scant 1/4 teaspoon of salt (optional) - 2 or 3 cups of ice water, for washing the butter instructions 1. culture the cream (optional): the day before you would like to make your butter, pour the cream into a bowl (i like to use the bowl of my stand mixer) and add the yogurt. whisk briefly to combine and cover the bowl with a clean kitchen towel. set in a slightly warm place (about 70°f - 75°f) to culture. check after 8 to 12 hours. the cream is ready when it has thickened slightly and is a little foamy. it will smell slightly sour and tangy. this can possibly take an additional 12 to 24 (see recipe notes). once it has cultured, place it in the refrigerator for about 1 hour to chill.→ if you did not culture your butter, let it warm on the counter for about an hour (to about 60°f) before churning. 2. prepare the sieve and mixer: place a sturdy sieve over a bowl and line with a few layers of cheesecloth or a clean napkin. you can use a stand mixer, a hand mixer, a food processor, or a canning jar to churn your cream. (see recipe notes below if you want use a canning jar.) 3. prepare the cream and mixer for churning: place the cream in the bowl of your mixer or processor. cover the top with plastic wrap or a kitchen towel to prevent splattering. 4. churn the cream: turn on the mixer to medium-high. the cream will first whip into peaks (at around 2 minutes) and then become grainy (around 3 minutes). keep whipping until the solid mass (butter) and liquid (buttermilk) are separated (about 5 minutes total). the mixture will splatter heavily in the final stages of churning, so be sure the plastic wrap is secure. the process may take a little longer, up to 8 to 10 minutes, although it usually takes me less than 5 minutes. 5. strain off the buttermilk: pour the buttermilk through the cheesecloth and strainer, holding the butter solid back. allow the buttermilk to strain through, then plop in the butter. gather the cloth around the butter and press it hard with your fist. do this several times to get as much buttermilk out of the butter as possible. pour the buttermilk into a container, label and refrigerate. 6. wash the butter: rinse out the bowl used for buttermilk. remove the butter from the cloth and place it in the bowl. add 1/2 cup of ice water to the bowl, and using a spatula, press the butter into the ice water. it will quickly become cloudy with buttermilk. pour off the cloudy water, add another 1/2 cup of ice water to the bowl, and keep pressing. repeat until the water is clear. this may take up to 6 washings. the butter will firm up towards the end, so you may find it easier to use your hands. 7. salt the butter (optional): sprinkle the salt over the butter and knead in. again, your hands may be the best tool here. 8. store the butter. pack the butter into a jar with a cover, or roll it into a log using waxed paper or parchment paper. the butter will keep in the refrigerator for about three weeks or can be frozen for several months. 9. notes on culturing: many factors will influence how long the cream takes to culture: ambient room temperature, how your cream was processed and pasteurized, how your yogurt was processed and pasteurized, etc. if the cream cultures too quickly and you're not ready to make the butter yet, simply put it into the refrigerator until you are ready. just be sure you remove it about an hour before churning so that it can warm up a bit.cultured cream will be thickened and slightly foamy, and it will have a somewhat tangy, almost yogurt-like smell. trust your senses! if you feel it is too strong and has gone bad, just throw it away. but remember that the yogurt is introducing beneficial cultures that help prevent spoilage, so the likelihood of this happening is small.unplugged butter: you can skip the electric mixer/processor and simply shake your cream in a covered canning jar or well-sealed container until it forms into the butter mass. this can take a while, up to 20 minutes or more, so be prepared for a work-out or solicit some help.recipe can easily be doubled.

title: How To Make Sourdough Cardamom Buns
text: how to make sourdough cardamom buns source: breadbyelise.com ingredients - 45 g active sourdough starter (100% hydration, white) - 45 g whole milk (cold) - 45 g all-purpose or bread flour - 10 g sugar - 550 g bread flour (11-13% protein) - 90 g sugar - 10 g salt - 2 g ground cardamom ((1 tsp)) - 250 g whole milk (cold) - 2 eggs (small-medium sized) - 145 g sweet levain - 110 g unsalted butter (softened, cut into cubes) - 100 g unsalted butter (softened) - 90 g brown sugar - 2,5 g ground cardamom ((1,5 tsp)) - 50 g brown sugar - 50 g water - 1 g ground cardamom ((0,5 tsp)) instructions 1. start by mixing active sourdough starter, milk, flour, and sugar in a medium-sized bowl. cover and rise in a warm spot for 4 hours or until the levain has doubled/tripled in size. 2. start by gathering all the ingredients. add them all, except the butter, to the bowl of your stand mixer fitted with a dough hook. mix on medium speed until the dough comes together. cover, and autolyse/rest for 30 minutes. 3. start your mixer again and knead on medium speed for 5-10 minutes. 4. after 5-10 minutes: slowly add in the softened butter, one cube at a time. 5. when all the butter is added, continue kneading at medium speed for 15-25 minutes until your dough passes the window-pane test. 6. place the dough in a clean bowl and proof in a warm spot, ideally at around 78°f/26°c, for two hours. 7. after two hours, transfer the dough to the fridge to cold-proof for a minimum of six hours. 8. add softened butter, brown sugar, and cardamom to a bowl. mix with a fork until you have a spreadable paste. leave at room temperature until you're ready to shape the buns. 9. transfer the dough to a lightly floured work surface. you might want to leave it at room temperature for 10-15 minutes if it's really cold and difficult to roll out. 10. with a rolling pin, roll the dough into a 19x12in/50x30cm rectangle. 11. evenly spread out the cardamom filling using an offset spatula. 12. grab one of the long sides of the rectangle and fold it down to cover 2/3 of the dough, then grab the other side and fold it over the top (see pictures above for reference). 13. go over the dough a couple of times with a rolling pin to even out the sides. 14. use a sharp knife to cut the dough into 12 strips, roughly 1,5-2 inches each. 15. split each strip into three, leaving one side joined. braid the strips to create a three-stranded plait. grab the end of the plait and roll it up to create a bun—place all the shaped buns in a greased muffin tin. 16. loosely cover the muffin tin with cling film and proof at around 78°f/26°c for 9-12 hours until they've doubled in size. 17. preheat your oven to 355°f/180°c and bake the cardamom buns for 18-20 minutes until golden brown. meanwhile, you can make the brown sugar glaze: 18. while the buns are baking, you can make the glaze. add the ingredients to a small pot and heat up over medium heat until all the sugar is dissolved. 19. when the buns are out of the oven, immediately brush over the syrup using a pastry brush. transfer to a cooling rack and cool for 20-30 minutes before serving.

title: Sourdough Cardamom Buns
text: sourdough cardamom buns source: bread by elise ingredients - 45 g active sourdough starter 100% hydration, white - 45 g whole milk cold - 45 g all-purpose or bread flour - 10 g sugar - 550 g bread flour 11-13% protein - 90 g sugar - 10 g salt - 2 g ground cardamom (1 tsp) - 250 g whole milk cold - 2 eggs small-medium sized - 145 g sweet levain - 110 g unsalted butter softened, cut into cubes - 100 g unsalted butter softened - 90 g brown sugar - 2.5 g ground cardamom (1.5 tsp) - 50 g brown sugar - 50 g water - 1 g ground cardamom (0.5 tsp) instructions 1. mix active sourdough starter, milk, flour, and sugar in a medium-sized bowl, cover, and rise in a warm spot for 4 hours or until the levain has doubled or tripled in size. 2. add all main dough ingredients except the butter to the bowl of a stand mixer fitted with a dough hook and mix on medium speed until the dough comes together. 3. cover and autolyse the dough for 30 minutes. 4. start the mixer again and knead on medium speed for 5-10 minutes. 5. slowly add in the softened butter, one cube at a time, while the mixer is running. 6. continue kneading at medium speed for 15-25 minutes until the dough passes the window-pane test. 7. place the dough in a clean bowl and proof in a warm spot at around 78°f/26°c for two hours. 8. transfer the dough to the fridge to cold-proof for a minimum of six hours. 9. mix softened butter, brown sugar, and cardamom in a bowl until you have a spreadable paste and leave at room temperature until ready to shape the buns. 10. transfer the dough to a lightly floured work surface and leave at room temperature for 10-15 minutes if it is very cold and difficult to roll out. 11. roll the dough into a 19x12in/50x30cm rectangle with a rolling pin. 12. evenly spread out the cardamom filling using an offset spatula. 13. grab one of the long sides of the rectangle and fold it down to cover 2/3 of the dough, then grab the other side and fold it over the top. 14. go over the dough a couple of times with a rolling pin to even out the sides. 15. use a sharp knife to cut the dough into 12 strips, roughly 1.5-2 inches each. 16. split each strip into three, leaving one side joined, and braid the strips to create a three-stranded plait. 17. grab the end of the plait and roll it up to create a bun, then place all the shaped buns in a greased muffin tin. 18. loosely cover the muffin tin with cling film and proof at around 78°f/26°c for 9-12 hours until the buns have doubled in size. 19. preheat your oven to 355°f/180°c and bake the cardamom buns for 18-20 minutes until golden brown. 20. while the buns are baking, add brown sugar, water, and ground cardamom to a small pot and heat over medium heat until all the sugar is dissolved. 21. when the buns are out of the oven, immediately brush over the syrup using a pastry brush. 22. transfer to a cooling rack and cool for 20-30 minutes before serving.

title: Salt Crusted Chicken
text: salt crusted chicken source: paleoscaleo.com ingredients - 1 five pound chicken - 5 - 6 cups kosher salt - 1 1/2 cups water instructions 1. preheat the oven to 400° and line a baking sheet with parchment paper. 2. in a large bowl, combine the salt and water and stir until you have "wet sand." set aside. 3. using a sharp pair of kitchen shears, cut the backbone out of the chicken. (this is called "spatchcocking" and allows the chicken to cook more evenly.) 4. spread a small amount (1-2 handfuls) out on the parchment paper, and place the chicken on top, laying flat. 5. pile the rest of the salt mixture on top. pat it down like you're building a sandcastle, making sure it's completely coated, there are no holes, and no spots of skin peeking through. you're trying to achieve an even coating. 6. bake in the oven for 1 hour and 30 minutes. 7. remove from oven, and using a knife or mallet, break open the 'crust' the salt has formed over the chicken and discard. use a pastry brush to brush off any loose salt. 8. peel the skin off the chicken to reveal the juicy, tender, and perfectly cooked meat underneath. the skin will be very salty, but the meat underneath will not be. 9. serve immediately.

title: How to Make Almond Milk
text: how to make almond milk source: minimalistbaker.com ingredients - 1 cup raw almonds ((soaked overnight in cool water // or 1-2 hours in very hot water)) - 5 cups filtered water ((less to thicken, more to thin)) - 1 pinch sea salt - 2 whole dates ((optional // pitted // or other sweetener of choice // omit for unsweetened)) - 1 tsp vanilla extract ((optional // or sub 1 vanilla bean, scraped per 1 tsp extract // omit for plain)) - 2 tbsp cocoa powder ((optional // for "chocolate milk")) - 1/2 cup berries ((optional // for "berry milk")) instructions 1. add your soaked almonds, water, salt, and any additional add-ins (optional) to a high-speed blender and blend until creamy and smooth. keep it running for at least 1-2 minutes so you get the most out of your almonds. 2. strain using a nut milk bag or my favorite trick - a thin dish towel. simply lay a clean dish towel over a mixing bowl, pour over the almond milk, carefully gather the corners, and lift up. then squeeze until all of the liquid is extracted. discard pulp, or save for adding to baked goods (especially crackers). find more ways to use almond pulp here. 3. transfer milk to a jar or covered bottle and refrigerate. will keep for up to 4-5 days, though best when fresh. shake well before drinking, as it tends to separate.

title: How to Make Chicken Stock
text: how to make chicken stock source: simplyrecipes.com ingredients - leftover bones and skin from 1 large cooked or raw chicken carcass, or from 2 rotisserie chickens - celery tops and 1 large celery rib, cut into 2-inch segments - 1 large unpeeled onion, quartered - 1 carrot, cut into 2-inch segments - 1 bunch parsley (stems and leaves) - salt, to taste - black pepper, to taste - 1 tablespoon olive oil - 4 to 5 pounds chicken wings, backs and/or legs, skin-on, trimmed of excess fat, hacked with a cleaver into 2-inch pieces - 1 large rib celery plus 1 handful leafy celery tops, cut into 2-inch segments - leek or green onions (if you have them) - 1 bay leaf - 6 quarts cold water - 1 tablespoon salt, or to taste - 4 pounds chicken wings, backs, and/or legs, hacked with a cleaver into 2-inch pieces - 1 large onion, chopped - 2 quarts boiling water - 2 teaspoons salt, or to taste - 2 bay leaves instructions 1. put the leftover bones and skin from a chicken carcass into a large stock pot and add vegetables like celery, onion, carrots, and parsley, then cover with water and add salt and pepper to taste. 2. bring the stock to a boil and immediately reduce heat to bring it to barely a simmer, simmering partially covered for at least 4 hours while occasionally skimming off any foam that comes to the surface. 3. optionally reduce the stock by simmering an hour or two longer to make it more concentrated and easier to store. 4. remove the bones and vegetables with a slotted spoon or spider ladle, and strain the stock through a fine mesh sieve. 5. coat the bottom of a large stock pot with olive oil and place half of the chicken pieces skin side down in the bottom of the pot, heating on medium high until the chicken is browned. 6. add the rest of the chicken pieces and cook, occasionally stirring until the chicken is no longer pink. 7. add the onion, carrot, celery, parsley, leek or green onions if using, and bay leaf to the pot, then cover with 6 quarts of cold water. 8. bring to a boil on high heat and reduce to a low simmer, skimming off any scum that rises to the surface in the first half hour of cooking. 9. let simmer uncovered at a low simmer for 4 to 6 hours, checking every hour to ensure there is still enough water in the pot and lowering the heat or adding more water if needed. 10. use a large metal spoon with holes or a spider ladle to remove the cooked chicken and vegetables, and discard them. 11. use a large sieve lined with dampened cheesecloth or paper towel and place over a large bowl or pot, then pour the stock through the sieve to strain out any remaining solids. 12. pour the strained stock into jars or optionally boil on high heat for 1 hour to reduce by about half, then let cool completely before refrigerating or freezing, leaving at least 1-inch head space if freezing. 13. heat 1 tablespoon of olive oil in a large stock pot, add one chopped onion, and sauté until softened and slightly colored for 2 to 3 minutes, then transfer to a large bowl. 14. add half of the chicken pieces to the pot and sauté until no longer pink, about 4 to 5 minutes, then transfer to the bowl with the onions and repeat with the remaining chicken pieces. 15. return the onion and chicken pieces to the pot, reduce heat to low, cover, and cook until chicken releases its juices for about 20 minutes while simultaneously bringing 2 quarts of water to a boil in a large tea kettle. 16. after the chicken pieces have been cooking for 20 minutes, raise the heat to high, add the 2 quarts of boiling water, 2 teaspoons of salt, and 2 bay leaves. 17. return to a low simmer while scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan with a wooden spoon, then cover and barely simmer for about 20 minutes. 18. strain the stock through cheesecloth or paper towel-lined large sieve, discarding solids and removing the large pieces of bone with a slotted spoon first. 19. pour the strained stock into jars and cool completely before refrigerating or freezing, where it will last about a week in the refrigerator or several months in the freezer.

title: Japanese Soufflé Creme Brûlée Pancakes
text: japanese soufflé creme brûlée pancakes source: iamafoodblog.com ingredients - 6 tablespoons milk - 1 large egg yolk - 2 tablespoons sugar - 1 tablespoon flour - 2 tablespoons room temperature butter - 1 egg yolk - 1/2 tablespoon sugar - 2 tablespoons milk - 3 tablespoons flour - 1/4 teaspoon baking powder - 2 large egg whites - 1/8 teaspoon cream of tartar - 1 tablespoon sugar instructions 1. start by making the creme sauce by whisking together the egg yolk, sugar, and flour until smooth. 2. whisk in the milk and strain into a small pot. 3. heat over medium low heat until the custard thickens. 4. remove from the heat and stir in the butter and set aside. 5. whisk the egg yolk with 1 tablespoon of sugar until pale and frothy. 6. mix the milk in batches into the yolk mixture. 7. sift the flour and baking powder over the yolk mixture and whisk well making sure everything is incorporated. 8. whip the egg whites with the cream of tartar until frothy and pale, adding in the sugar a bit at a time until the whites are whipped into a glossy thick meringue that holds a peak. 9. take 1/3 of the whipped egg whites and whisk it into the bowl with the yolks until completely incorporated. 10. add half of the remaining whites and whisk into the yolk batter, being careful not to deflate. 11. transfer the egg yolk mixture to the remaining egg whites and fold together with a spatula. 12. heat up a large non stick frying pan with a lid and very lightly brush with oil. 13. using an ice cream scoop or measuring spoon, scoop about 1/4 cup batter onto the pan, leaving space in between and cover and cook for 3 minutes. 14. remove the lid and add some more batter on top of each pancake, cover and continue to cook for 4-5 more minutes. 15. lift the lid and use a spatula to gently peek under the pancake to check if it releases easily. 16. if you still have any batter left, pile it on top of the pancakes and then gently flip. 17. cover and cook for 5-6 minutes while making sure your creme sauce is loose and pourable, heating it gently with extra milk if needed. 18. once the pancakes are golden and cooked through, gently remove and pile onto a plate. 19. spoon the creme sauce on top and sprinkle generously with sugar. 20. use a cooking torch to brûlée the sugar and serve immediately.

title: Sticky Toffee Pudding
text: sticky toffee pudding source: the guardian ingredients - 50g unsalted butter, plus extra to grease - 175g medjool dates - 1 tsp bicarbonate of soda - 75g walnuts (optional) - 80g golden caster sugar - 80g dark muscovado sugar - 1 pinch salt - 2 cloves - 175g flour - 1 tsp baking powder - 2 eggs - 115g unsalted butter (for sauce) - 75g golden caster sugar (for sauce) - 40g dark muscovado sugar (for sauce) - 140ml double cream (for sauce) instructions 1. heat the oven to 200c (180c fan)/390f/gas 6 and soften the butter. stone and roughly chop the dates with a small, sharp knife. 2. put all sauce ingredients in a small pan over low heat until the butter melts, stirring regularly. turn up the heat and bring to a boil. simmer for about four minutes until thick enough to coat the back of a spoon. 3. grease a 24cm x 24cm baking dish with butter. pour half the sauce into the dish, tip it to coat the base completely, then place in the freezer. boil a kettle of water. 4. put the dates and bicarbonate of soda in a heatproof bowl and pour over 300ml boiling water to cover. leave to soften. if using walnuts, toast them in a dry frying pan over medium-high heat until fragrant, then roughly chop. 5. put the butter and both sugars into a large bowl or food mixer with a pinch of salt. beat vigorously until very light and fluffy. grind the cloves to a fine powder and whisk with the flour and baking powder in a separate bowl. beat the eggs in a cup or jug. 6. beat the eggs into the butter and sugar mixture a little at a time until thoroughly incorporated. fold in the dry ingredients with a large metal spoon, being careful not to knock out too much air. finally, fold in the dates with their soaking water and the walnuts if using. 7. take the dish out of the freezer and pour the batter on top of the sauce. level out the batter and bake for about 30 minutes until just firm to the touch in the centre. reheat the remaining sauce in the pan towards the end of cooking. 8. heat the grill to medium. poke small holes across the top of the baked pudding with a skewer, then pour the sauce over the top. put the dish under the grill until the top is molten and bubbling, watching carefully so the sugar doesn't burn. 9. serve immediately with ice-cream, custard, crème fraîche or greek yoghurt. alternatively, bake the pudding ahead of time without the remaining sauce, cover with foil, reheat in a 180c (160c fan)/350f/gas 4 oven for about 20 minutes, then continue with the grilling step.

title: How to make sticky toffee pudding – recipe | Felicity Cloake’s masterclass
text: how to make sticky toffee pudding – recipe | felicity cloake’s masterclass ingredients instructions <https://www.theguardian.com/food/2019/feb/27/sticky-toffee-pudding-recipe-felicity-cloake-masterclass?cmp=sharebtnlink --- felicity cloake’s sticky toffee pudding. photograph: dan matthews/the guardian. food styling: loïc parisot. view image in fullscreen felicity cloake’s sticky toffee pudding. photograph: dan matthews/the guardian. food styling: loïc parisot. how to make sticky toffee pudding – recipe is there anything more comforting than a sticky toffee pudding? here’s your step-by-step guide to a faultless dessert sticky toffee pudding: the very name is enough to gladden the heart, if not the waistband. this ‘british classic’, famous around the world thanks to a namecheck in harry potter, is actually a relatively recent invention, probably with canadian origins, popularised by a lake district hotel in the 1970s. though unapologetically sweet, it’s surprisingly light – until you add a big dollop of ice-cream, of course. view image in fullscreen prep 25 min cook 35 min serves 6 50g unsalted butter, plus extra to grease 175g medjool dates 1 tsp bicarbonate of soda 75g walnuts (optional) 80g golden caster sugar 80g dark muscovado sugar 1 pinch salt 2 cloves 175g flour 1 tsp baking powder 2 eggs for the sauce 115g unsalted butter 75g golden caster sugar 40g dark muscovado sugar 140ml double cream 1 prep the dates heat the oven to 200c (180c fan)/390f/gas 6) and get the butter out of the fridge to soften, if you haven’t already. stone and roughly chop the dates – though sticky, this process should be relatively easy with a small, sharp knife. medjool dates are softer and richer in flavour than some other common varieties, so are the best ones to use for this recipe, if you can find them. 2 make the sauce put all the ingredients for the sauce in a small pan. put over a low heat until the butter melts, stirring regularly to encourage it, then mix together, turn up the heat and bring to a boil. simmer for about four minutes, until the sauce is thick enough to coat the back of a spoon. view image in fullscreen make the sauce by melting together butter, caster and muscovado sugar, and cream. 3 line the dish grease a 24cm x 24cm baking dish with butter. pour half the sauce into the prepared dish, tip it this way and that until the base is completely coated, then put the dish in the freezer while you make the batter. leave the rest of the sauce in the pan for now. boil a kettle of water. 4 prepare the dates and nuts put the dates and bicarb in a heatproof bowl and pour over 300ml boiling water to cover. leave them to soften while you get the rest of the batter ingredients ready. view image in fullscreen put stoned and chopped dates in a bowl with a little bicarb, cover with boiling water and leave to soak. if you’re using the walnuts (pecans would also be nice), heat a small, dry frying pan over a medium-high heat, toast them until fragrant, then tip out on to a board and roughly chop. 5 start on the batter view image in fullscreen prepare the batter: butter, sugars, flour, baking powder, eggs and a pinch of salt. put the butter and both sugars into a large bowl or food mixer, add a pinch of salt, then beat vigorously until very light and fluffy. grind the cloves to a fine powder and, in a separate bowl, whisk with the flour and baking powder. beat the eggs in a cup or jug. 6 finish the batter view image in fullscreen add the dates and walnuts to the batter, and fold in gently, so as not to knock out too much air. beat the eggs, a little at a time, into the butter and sugar mixture, until thoroughly incorporated, then use a large metal spoon to fold in the dry ingredients, being careful to knock as little air out of the mixture as possible. finally, fold in the dates and their soaking water, plus the walnuts, if using. 7 bake take the dish out of the freezer and pour the batter on top of the sauce. tip the dish to level out the batter, then bake for about 30 minutes, until just firm to the touch in the centre. towards the end of the cooking time, reheat the remaining sauce in the pan. view image in fullscreen put half the sauce in a baking dish and chill. top with batter and bake, then pour on the rest of the sauce and grill . 8 grill the top heat the grill to medium. using a skewer or similar, poke small holes all across the top of the baked pudding, then pour the sauce over the top. remembering it will still be hot, put the dish under the grill until the top is molten and bubbling – keeping a watchful eye on it, because sugar is quick to burn. 9 serve (or reheat) serve the sticky toffee pudding immediately, with ice-cream, custard, creme fraiche or greek yoghurt. alternatively, bake the pudding itself ahead of time, but don’t add the remaining sauce until you’re ready to serve. cover the pudding with foil, then reheat in a 180c (160c fan)/350f/gas 4 oven for about 20 minutes, then continue with step 8. explore more on these topics - food - felicity cloake's masterclass - dessert - features reuse this content

title: Hungarian Goulash
text: hungarian goulash source: spendwithpennies.com ingredients - 2 teaspoons salted butter, oil, or lard - 2 medium yellow onions, diced - 1 teaspoon caraway seeds - 2 tablespoons paprika - 1½ pounds stewing beef or chuck, trimmed and cut into 1-inch cubes - 2 tablespoons all-purpose flour - 2 cups beef broth or water - 1 cup canned diced tomatoes, drained - 1 teaspoon salt or to taste - ¼ teaspoon black pepper - 2 medium potatoes, peeled and diced (optional) - 3 medium carrots, diced (optional) - chopped fresh parsley and sour cream for serving (optional) instructions 1. in a dutch oven or large pot, melt the butter over medium-low heat, add the onion and cook until translucent about 5 minutes, then stir in caraway seeds and paprika. 2. in a bowl or zip-top bag, dredge the beef with flour and shake off any excess, then add the beef to the onion mixture and cook for 2-3 minutes. 3. slowly add ¼ cup of beef broth while scraping up any brown bits from the bottom of the pan, then add the remaining broth and diced tomatoes, and add potatoes and carrots if using, and season with salt and black pepper. 4. bring to a boil over medium-high heat, then reduce the heat to a low simmer, cover, and cook for about 1½ to 2 hours or until the beef is fork-tender. 5. garnish with parsley if desired and serve with a dollop of sour cream.

title: Kohlrabi Soup with Kohlrabi Greens
text: kohlrabi soup with kohlrabi greens source: chocolatemoosey.com ingredients - 1 tablespoon olive oil - salt (preferably kosher), to taste - 1/4 cup diced white or yellow onion - 1 large carrot, peeled and diced - 1 clove garlic, minced - 5 cups vegetable broth/stock - 1 pound kohlrabi, bulbs peeled and diced and leaves chopped - 1 small sweet potato, peeled and diced (roughly 8 ounces) - 1 tablespoon lemon juice instructions 1. in a dutch oven or large pot, add the oil. once hot, add the onion, carrot, and a big pinch of salt. cook until they start to soften and brown, about 3-5 minutes. add the garlic and cook 1 minute. 2. add 1 + 1/2 cups broth and bring to a boil. cook until carrots are softened, about 8-10 minutes. 3. transfer mixture to a blender and blend until smooth. there should be enough broth but if it's too thick to blend, you can add a little more. 4. pour the carrot puree back into the dutch oven. add the remaining 3 + 1/2 cups broth then bring to a boil. 5. once boiling, add the kohlrabi bulbs, sweet potato, and a big pinch of salt. cook until fork tender, about 15 minutes.you should have enough broth, but if your vegetable amounts are bigger than indicated, it's possible you may need to add more as the vegetables will absorb the broth. 6. add kohlrabi leaves and cook 3-5 minutes until the leaves are softened. add lemon juice then taste and adjust for salt.

title: Hungarian Plum Cake
text: hungarian plum cake source: cookpad.com ingredients - 4 medium eggs - 190g butter - 190g cane sugar - 1 large pinch salt - 125g plain yogurt - 12g baking powder - 190g whole grain spelt flour - 1 teaspoon ground cinnamon - 350g plum preserve - ground cinnamon for topping - 100g granulated sugar - 30g coarsely chopped walnuts instructions 1. melt the butter slightly, add the sugar and mix, then add the egg yolks and yogurt and mix well. 2. add the cinnamon and the flour mixed with sifted baking powder and mix together. 3. beat the egg whites until stiff and fold them into the batter carefully little by little. 4. pour the batter into a buttered and floured 21x31 cm baking pan, then place the halved plums on top and sprinkle with cinnamon. 5. bake in a preheated oven at 180 degrees c for 40-45 minutes until a skewer inserted into the centre comes out clean, covering the top with foil halfway through to prevent over-browning. 6. while the cake bakes, prepare the praline by melting the sugar in a pot over heat, stirring constantly until it becomes light brown, then add the walnuts and stir. 7. pour the hot praline onto an oiled board, roll it thinly with an oiled rolling pin, cut it into pieces, and sprinkle over the baked cake brushed with plum jam.

title: Indian Barfi Fudge
text: indian barfi fudge ingredients - 3 cups milk powder - 1 1/2 cups powdered sugar - 1/2 cup plus 3 tablespoons milk - 3 tablespoons butter or ghee - 1/2 to 1 teaspoon ground cardamom - 1/4 teaspoon salt - 1 teaspoon vanilla extract - approximately 2 tablespoons slivered pistachios - saffron, rose buds, and silver leaf for garnish instructions 1. grease a 9×6 baking pan. 2. heat a heavy bottom pan on medium to low heat and add the butter and 1/2 cup of milk, allowing the butter to melt. 3. once the butter melts, add the milk powder while stirring constantly, then gradually add the powdered sugar. 4. if dry powder bits remain, add the three tablespoons of milk one tablespoon at a time until the mixture reaches a paste-like consistency. 5. while continuously stirring, cook the mixture for 8–9 minutes until it easily leaves the surface of the pan and resembles dough. 6. turn off the heat and add vanilla extract, cardamom, and a tablespoon of pistachios, then mix well. 7. spread the mixture evenly on the greased pan and top with the remaining tablespoon of pistachios. 8. let the barfi set for at least three hours before serving or storing in an airtight container at room temperature for up to seven days.

title: Italian Marinade
text: italian marinade source: unknown ingredients - 1 cup extra-virgin olive oil - 3/4 cup red wine vinegar - zest of 1 lemon - 1/4 cup freshly squeezed lemon juice (about 2 lemons) - 4 cloves garlic, peeled, smashed and roughly chopped - 1 bay leaf - 1 tablespoon thyme leaves - 1 tablespoon oregano leaves - 1 tablespoon basil leaves, rolled and chopped into chiffonade - 1 teaspoon granulated sugar - 1 teaspoon kosher salt - 1 teaspoon freshly cracked black pepper - 1 teaspoon red pepper flakes, or to taste instructions 1. combine the olive oil, red wine vinegar, lemon zest, lemon juice, garlic, bay leaf, thyme, oregano, basil, sugar, salt, pepper, and red pepper flakes in a bowl and whisk until well blended.

title: Jacques Torres Chocolate Chip Cookies
text: jacques torres chocolate chip cookies ingredients - 2 cups (240g) cake flour - 2 cups (240g) bread flour - 1 1/2 teaspoons baking powder - 1 1/4 teaspoons baking soda - 1 1/2 teaspoons salt - 1 1/4 cups (282g) unsalted butter, softened - 1 1/4 cups plus 3 tablespoons (284g) firmly packed light brown sugar - 1 cup plus 2 tablespoons (227g) granulated sugar - 2 large eggs - 2 teaspoons vanilla extract - 1 1/4 pounds (567g) bittersweet chocolate discs (about 60% cacao) - sea salt instructions 1. thoroughly whisk together or sift the cake flour, bread flour, baking powder, baking soda, and salt, then set aside. 2. using a mixer with the paddle attachment, beat the butter, brown sugar, and sugar until light and fluffy, about 5 minutes. 3. add the eggs one at a time, mixing well after each addition. 4. mix in the vanilla. 5. reduce mixer speed to low and add the flour mixture, mixing just until combined, about 10 seconds. 6. stir in the chocolate discs, trying not to break them. 7. cover the dough with plastic wrap, pressing the plastic directly against the dough, and chill for 24 to 72 hours. 8. preheat oven to 350°f and line baking sheets with parchment paper or silicone liner. 9. divide the dough into 3 1/2 ounce (99g) portions using a #14 or #16 scoop to get about 1/4 cup of dough and adjusting with your scale as needed. 10. place the mounds of dough on the prepared pans, spacing about 6 cookies per pan or 4 at a time for more spreading room. 11. sprinkle the top of each cookie with a pinch of sea salt. 12. bake for 18 to 20 minutes, or until golden brown but still soft. 13. cool the cookies on the pans on a wire rack for 10 minutes. 14. transfer the cookies to a rack to cool completely.

title: Jacques Torres Chocolate Chip Cookies
text: jacques torres chocolate chip cookies source: bakeorbreak.com ingredients - 2 cups cake flour - 2 cups bread flour - 1 1/2 teaspoons teaspoons baking powder - 1 1/4 teaspoons teaspoons baking soda - 1 1/2 teaspoons teaspoons salt - 1 1/4 cups unsalted butter (softened) - 1 1/2 cups firmly packed light brown sugar (scant (1 1/4 cups + 3 tablespoons)) - 1 1/8 cup granulated sugar - 2 large eggs - 2 teaspoons vanilla extract - 1 1/4 pounds bittersweet chocolate discs (about 60% cacao) - sea salt instructions 1. thoroughly whisk together (or sift) the cake flour, bread flour, baking powder, baking soda, and salt. set aside. 2. using a mixer with the paddle attachment, beat the butter, brown sugar, and sugar until light and fluffy (about 5 minutes). add the eggs, one at a time, mixing well after each addition. mix in the vanilla. 3. reduce mixer speed to low. add the flour mixture, mixing just until combined (about 10 seconds). stir in the chocolate discs, trying not to break them. 4. cover the dough with plastic wrap, pressing the plastic directly against the dough. chill for 24 to 72 hours. 5. preheat oven to 350°f (175°c). line baking sheets with parchment paper or silicone liner. 6. divide the dough into 3.5 ounce (99g) portions. (use a #14 or #16 scoop to get about 1/4 cup of dough and use your scale to adjust.) place the mounds of dough on the prepared pans. (you can get about 6 cookies on a pan, but i often just bake 4 at a time to give them a little more space to spread.) sprinkle the top of each cookie with a pinch of sea salt. 7. bake 18 to 20 minutes, or until golden brown but still soft. 8. cool on the pans on a wire rack for 10 minutes. then transfer the cookies to a rack to cool completely.

title: Coffee Liqueur
text: coffee liqueur source: america's test kitchen ingredients - 1/2 cup medium-roast coffee beans - 1 1/2 teaspoons cacao nibs - 1/4 vanilla bean, halved lengthwise - 8 ounces vodka - 4 ounces brandy - 4 ounces simple syrup instructions 1. place coffee beans, cacao nibs, vanilla bean, vodka, and brandy in a pint-size glass jar, cover tightly, and shake to combine. 2. store the jar in a cool, dark place for 1 week, shaking the mixture once every other day. 3. set a fine-mesh strainer in a medium bowl and line it with a triple layer of cheesecloth. 4. strain the vodka mixture through the prepared strainer and discard the solids. 5. return the infused strained vodka mixture to a clean jar and add the simple syrup. 6. cover and gently shake to combine. 7. store in a cool, dark place for up to 1 year, shaking gently before using.

title: Karaage (Japanese Fried Chicken)
text: karaage (japanese fried chicken) source: justonecookbook.com ingredients - 1½ lb boneless, skin-on chicken thighs ((4–6 pieces; read the blog post for details)) - ½ tsp diamond crystal kosher salt - ⅛ tsp freshly ground black pepper - ½ tsp ginger ((grated, with juice)) - 1 clove garlic - ½–1 tbsp soy sauce - ½ tbsp sake ((or substitute dry sherry, chinese rice wine, or skip it)) - ½ tsp toasted sesame oil - 3–4 cups neutral oil - 2 tbsp potato starch or cornstarch ((plus more, if needed)) - 2 tbsp all-purpose flour (plain flour) ((plus more, if needed)) - lemon wedges - japanese kewpie mayonnaise - shichimi togarashi (japanese seven spice) instructions 1. before you start…please note that this recipe requires 30 minutes of marinating time. gather all the ingredients. 2. prepare 1½ lb boneless, skin-on chicken thighs by cutting each into 2-inch (5-cm) pieces. season with ½ tsp diamond crystal kosher salt and ⅛ tsp freshly ground black pepper. 3. now, grate the ginger (i use a ceramic grater) and measure ½ tsp ginger (grated, with juice). add it to a large bowl. mince or press 1 clove garlic (i use a garlic press) and add it to the bowl. 4. add ½–1 tbsp soy sauce, ½ tbsp sake, and ½ tsp toasted sesame oil to the ginger and garlic. whisk to combine. 5. add the chicken to the marinade and mix it with your hands. cover and marinate in the refrigerator for 30 minutes. 6. while the chicken is marinating, prepare the oil for deep-frying. pour about 3–4 cups neutral oil into a heavy-bottomed pot (i like using the 2.75-qt staub), until you have at least 1 to 1½ inches (2.5 to 3.8 cm) of oil. heat it to 325ºf (160ºc) over medium-low heat so you have enough time to prep the chicken. 7. meanwhile, dredge the chicken pieces. prepare separate piles of 2 tbsp all-purpose flour (plain flour) and 2 tbsp potato starch or cornstarch in a tray. lightly coat a piece of marinated chicken in the flour and dust off the excess. 8. next, dredge it in the potato starch and shake off the excess. place it in a separate tray. continue with the remaining chicken pieces. 9. check that the oil temperature has reached 325ºf (160ºc). tip: if you don‘t have an instant read thermometer, insert a wooden chopstick into the oil; you‘ll know it‘s hot enough if small bubbles start to appear around the tip. for more helpful tips, see my post how to deep-fry food.when it's ready, gently add 3 to 5 chicken pieces at a time to the hot oil. do not overcrowd the pot. tip: if you add too many pieces at once, the oil temperature will drop quickly, and the chicken will absorb too much oil. 10. deep-fry for 90 seconds, or until the chicken is a light golden color. transfer to a wire rack to drain the excess oil. tip: if the chicken browns too quickly, then the oil temperature is too high. either put a few more pieces of chicken in the oil or lower the heat setting. controlling the oil temperature at all times is very important for deep-frying. 11. the residual heat will continue to cook the chicken as it rests. continue to fry the remaining chicken pieces. between batches, scoop up and discard the crumbs in the oil with a fine-mesh sieve. this keeps the oil clean and prevents it from becoming darker. 12. now, raise the oil temperature to 350ºf (180ºc). place the first 3 to 5 pieces of rested chicken back into the oil and deep-fry for 45 seconds, or until the skin is golden brown and crispy. transfer them to the wire rack to drain the excess oil. continue frying the remaining chicken pieces. 13. the left photo shows the chicken pieces after the first fry and the right photo shows them after the second fry. the chicken pieces on the right are slightly darker in color. 14. serve the chicken hot with lemon wedges and a dipping plate of japanese kewpie mayonnaise. you can also sprinkle shichimi togarashi (japanese seven spice) on the mayo for a bit of spice, if desired. 15. let it cool completely and transfer to an airtight container. you can store it in the refrigerator for up to 3 days and in the freezer for up to a month.

title: Kasha
text: kasha ingredients - 1 cup kasha (buckwheat groats), coated in 1 egg - 2 cups boiling liquid (water and osem seasoning or broth) - 1 large onion, thinly sliced - 200–250 g mushrooms, sliced - 100–120 g egg noodles (dry) - olive oil or schmaltz - salt, to taste - black pepper instructions 1. heat oil in a wide pan and cook onions over medium-low heat until deeply golden. 2. add mushrooms and sauté until their liquid evaporates and they brown, then push to the side. 3. add egg-coated kasha to the pan, stir and toast for 1–2 minutes until dry, fragrant, and grains separate. 4. pour in 2 cups boiling liquid, stir once, cover, and cook on low for 10–12 minutes until absorbed. 5. meanwhile, boil egg noodles until just tender and drain well. 6. turn off heat, let kasha rest 5 minutes covered, then gently fold in noodles. 7. add salt as needed, lots of black pepper, and a drizzle of olive oil, then toss gently.

title: How To Make the Very Best Sweet Cornbread
text: how to make the very best sweet cornbread source: kitchn.com ingredients - 2 sticks (225g) + 2 tbsp unsalted butter, divided - 2 cups yellow cornmeal - 2 cups all-purpose flour - 2 tsp baking powder - 1 tsp baking soda - 1 tsp salt - 2 cups buttermilk - 2 large eggs - ½ cup brown sugar - ¼ cup + 2 tbsp honey, divided instructions 1. preheat oven to 375°f and melt 2 tbsp butter in a 9x13 baking pan in the oven while it preheats. 2. melt the remaining 2 sticks of butter in a saucepan or microwave and let cool slightly. 3. in a large bowl, whisk together cornmeal, flour, baking powder, baking soda, and salt. 4. in a separate bowl, whisk together buttermilk, eggs, brown sugar, and ¼ cup honey, then whisk in the melted butter. 5. pour wet ingredients into dry ingredients and stir until just combined, being careful not to overmix. 6. pour batter into the hot buttered pan and drizzle remaining 2 tbsp honey over the top. 7. bake for 25–30 minutes, until golden and a toothpick comes out clean.

title: Kohlrabi Pickles
text: kohlrabi pickles ingredients - 3 cups kohlrabi, peeled and cut into sticks - 2 medium carrots, peeled and cut into sticks - 1 clove garlic - 1 bay leaf - ¾ cup white vinegar - 1¼ cups water - 3 tbsp sugar - 1 tbsp pickling spice mix - 1 tsp salt - ¼ tsp red pepper flakes instructions 1. pack the kohlrabi sticks, carrot sticks, garlic clove, and bay leaf into a clean quart-sized mason jar. 2. in a small saucepan, combine vinegar, water, sugar, spice mix, salt, and red pepper flakes, and bring to a boil while stirring until sugar and salt dissolve. 3. pour the hot brine over the vegetables in the jar, making sure they are fully submerged. 4. let cool to room temperature, then seal and refrigerate until ready after 24 hours.
