title: Latvian Cold Beet Soup
text: latvian cold beet soup ingredients - 3 medium beets, cooked, peeled, and grated or diced - 3–4 cucumbers, diced - 4–5 green onions, sliced - bunch of fresh dill, chopped - 1 liter kefir or buttermilk - 1 tbsp horseradish or mustard - salt and pepper, to taste - 2–4 hard-boiled eggs, halved - cold boiled water, to thin as needed - 2 tbsp lemon juice - 100g sour cream instructions 1. cook beets until tender by boiling or roasting, then let cool, peel, and grate or dice. 2. combine beets, cucumbers, green onions, and dill in a large bowl. 3. pour in kefir or buttermilk and stir in horseradish or mustard, lemon juice, salt, and pepper. 4. add cold boiled water to reach desired consistency and stir well, tasting for seasoning. 5. refrigerate until thoroughly chilled and serve cold, topped with hard-boiled egg halves and a dollop of sour cream.

title: Lekvar (Prune Butter)
text: lekvar (prune butter) ingredients - prunes - water - orange zest - orange juice - sugar - nuts (optional) instructions 1. in a small pot, add the prunes and water and bring to a boil over medium heat. 2. once the water boils, turn the heat down and simmer for 5 to 7 minutes to soften the prunes. 3. using a strainer or a slotted spoon, remove the prunes and place them in a mixing bowl or a mini food processor, reserving the prune water. 4. place the prunes, orange zest and juice, sugar and 2 teaspoons of the reserved prune water in the bowl of a mini food processor. 5. pulse until mostly smooth, a few pieces of prune are acceptable. 6. if using a hand blender or potato masher, put all ingredients in a bowl and proceed to blend. 7. taste for flavor and notice the texture. 8. if it seems too thick to use easily, add the third teaspoon of the prune water. 9. if using nuts, place the mixture in a bowl and mix in nuts, adding about half and adjusting to taste.

title: Lekvar (Prune Filling or Prune Butter)
text: lekvar (prune filling or prune butter) ingredients - 2 cups dried prunes - 1 cup water - 1/4 cup orange juice - 1 tablespoon lemon juice - 1/2 teaspoon salt - 1 dash clove - 1 dash cinnamon - 1/3 cup brown sugar instructions 1. combine prunes, water, orange juice, lemon juice, salt, clove, and cinnamon into a saucepan and cook on low heat, stirring every few minutes until the mixture reaches a boil. 2. lower heat to simmer, cover the pan, and cook for 20 minutes, stirring every few minutes. 3. remove the lid from the pan and add brown sugar, then cook while reducing the liquid and stirring every few minutes, being careful not to scorch the mixture. 4. mash the mixture with a wooden spoon until the prunes are soft and broken up and the consistency resembles oatmeal, about 20 more minutes, then allow to cool as it will thicken further.

title: Lemon Buttermilk Muffins with Greek Yogurt & Honey
text: lemon buttermilk muffins with greek yogurt & honey ingredients - 200 ml buttermilk - 60 g oat flakes - 200 g wholemeal flour (e.g., spelt) - 2 eggs - 2 tsp regular baking powder - 80 g whole cane sugar - 1 tsp pure vanilla extract - 100 ml canola oil - 2 organic lemons (zest and juice) - 2–3 tsp full-fat greek yogurt (10%) - 1 tbsp honey instructions 1. preheat your oven to 180°c (fan/convection) and place paper muffin liners in your tray. 2. wash the lemons, grate the zest, then squeeze out the juice and set both aside. 3. in a bowl, mix buttermilk, oat flakes, and lemon zest and let it sit for about 5–10 minutes to soften. 4. slice the vanilla pod and scrape out the seeds, or use vanilla extract. 5. beat the eggs, then stir in the soaked oat mixture, sugar, vanilla, canola oil, and lemon juice. 6. in a separate bowl, whisk together the wholemeal flour and baking powder, then add to the wet mixture and stir until just combined without overmixing. 7. divide the batter evenly between the muffin cups and bake on the middle rack for 20–25 minutes, or until golden brown and a toothpick comes out clean. 8. let the muffins cool in the tray for 5 minutes, then remove and cool completely on a rack. 9. in a small bowl, mix greek yogurt with honey until smooth and spoon or pipe a little on top of each muffin before serving.

title: Lemon Buttermilk Muffins with Greek Yogurt & Honey
text: lemon buttermilk muffins with greek yogurt & honey ingredients - 200 ml buttermilk - 60 g oat flakes - 200 g wholemeal flour - 2 eggs - 2 tsp baking powder - 80 g whole cane sugar - 1 tsp pure vanilla extract - 100 ml canola oil - 2 organic lemons (zest and juice) - 2–3 tsp full-fat greek yogurt (10%) - 1 tbsp honey instructions 1. preheat your oven to 180°c (fan/convection) and place paper muffin liners in your tray. 2. wash the lemons, grate the zest, then squeeze out the juice and set both aside. 3. in a bowl, mix buttermilk, oat flakes, and lemon zest and let it sit for about 5–10 minutes to soften. 4. beat the eggs, then stir in the soaked oat mixture, sugar, vanilla, canola oil, and lemon juice. 5. in a separate bowl, whisk together the wholemeal flour and baking powder. 6. add the dry mixture to the wet mixture and stir until just combined without overmixing. 7. divide the batter evenly between the muffin cups. 8. bake on the middle rack for 20–25 minutes, or until golden brown and a toothpick comes out clean. 9. let the muffins cool in the tray for 5 minutes, then remove and cool completely on a rack. 10. in a small bowl, mix greek yogurt with honey until smooth. 11. spoon or pipe a little of the topping on top of each muffin before serving.

title: Lemon Pound Cake
text: lemon pound cake source: once upon a chef ingredients - 3 cups all-purpose flour, spooned into measuring cup and leveled-off - 1/2 teaspoon baking soda - 1/2 teaspoon salt - 1 cup buttermilk - 2 tablespoons packed grated lemon zest - 2 tablespoons fresh lemon juice - 1 cup unsalted butter, softened - 2 1/4 cups granulated sugar - 3 large eggs - 2 tablespoons water - 2 tablespoons granulated sugar - 2 teaspoons fresh lemon juice - 1 cup confectioners' sugar - 2 tablespoons fresh lemon juice instructions 1. preheat the oven to 350°f and set an oven rack in the middle position. 2. spray two 8½ x 4½-inch loaf pans with nonstick cooking spray and line the long sides with parchment paper slings, then spray again. 3. in a medium bowl, whisk together the flour, baking soda, and salt, then set aside. 4. in another bowl, whisk together the buttermilk, lemon zest, and lemon juice, then set aside. 5. in the bowl of an electric mixer fitted with the paddle attachment, cream the butter and sugar on medium speed until light and fluffy, about 3 to 4 minutes. 6. beat in the eggs one at a time, beating well after each addition and scraping down the sides of the bowl. 7. with the mixer on low speed, alternate adding the flour and buttermilk mixtures, beginning and ending with the flour, then scrape down the sides and mix to ensure all ingredients are well-incorporated. 8. divide the batter into the prepared pans and smooth with a rubber spatula. 9. bake for 55 to 65 minutes, or until the top is golden and a tester comes out clean. 10. cool the cakes in the pans on a wire rack for 10 minutes, then carefully lift them out using the parchment slings and cool for about 1 hour more. 11. combine the water and sugar in a saucepan and bring to a boil, then remove from heat and stir in the lemon juice. 12. in a medium bowl, whisk together the confectioners' sugar and lemon juice until smooth, adjusting with more sugar or juice as needed for your preferred consistency. 13. brush the warm syrup all over the cooled cakes, including the sides, letting it soak in as you go. 14. spoon the glaze over the top of the cakes, letting it drip down the sides, and let sit for about 1 hour to allow the glaze to set before serving.

title: Margarita
text: margarita ingredients - 50 cc blanco tequila - 30 cc lime juice - 20 cc triple sec instructions 1. combine all ingredients in shaker tin. 2. add ice to small shaker tin. 3. shake vigorously. 4. strain into chilled rocks glass with a salt rim over fresh ice. 5. garnish with lime and enjoy.

title: Mac Pasta
text: mac pasta ingredients - 1/4 cup olive oil - 1 shallot - 1 garlic clove - 1/2 cup tomato paste - 2 tablespoons vodka - 1 cup heavy cream - 1 teaspoon red pepper flakes - salt and pepper to taste - 1 lb fusilli or linguini - 2 tablespoons unsalted butter - parmesan cheese - fresh basil instructions 1. heat olive oil in a dutch oven or cast iron pan. 2. add shallot and garlic and wait until softened. 3. add tomato paste and cook until it starts to caramelize. 4. add vodka and cook until all liquid has evaporated. 5. add heavy cream and stir until the sauce reaches an orange color, then turn off heat. 6. cook pasta for 3 minutes less than the package cooking time. 7. add cooked pasta to the sauce and stir so all pasta is evenly coated. 8. stir in butter and red pepper flakes. 9. serve with lots of chopped fresh basil.

title: Magic Three Layer Custard Cake
text: magic three layer custard cake source: recipetineats.com ingredients - 4 eggs, yolks and whites separated (at room temperature) - 3/4 cup (150g) sugar - 1 tsp vanilla extract - 1 stick (125g) unsalted butter, melted - 3/4 cup (115g) plain all purpose flour - 2 cups (500 ml) milk, lukewarm (full fat or low fat but not zero fat) - icing sugar (powdered sugar), for dusting - fresh strawberries, for serving - whipped cream, for serving instructions 1. preheat oven to 325f/160c. 2. butter an 8" x 8" square cake tin. 3. beat egg whites with a mixer until stiff peaks form and set aside. 4. place the egg yolks and sugar in a bowl and beat until pale yellow, about 1 minute. 5. add the vanilla extract and melted butter and beat until well incorporated. 6. add the flour and beat until just combined. 7. pour the milk in slowly while beating until well combined. 8. use a spatula to fold in the egg whites one third at a time until just incorporated. 9. pour the batter into the prepared cake tin. 10. bake until the top is golden brown and the cake does not jiggle when gently shaken, around 40 to 50 minutes. 11. check the cake at 30 minutes and if the top is golden brown but the cake jiggles, cover loosely with foil and return to the oven for 10 minutes at a time until set. 12. allow the cake to cool in the tin for 10 minutes, then turn out onto a cooling rack and cool completely. 13. cut into squares and dust with icing sugar just before serving. 14. serve with whipped cream and strawberries if desired.

title: Make Your Own Herbes de Provence
text: make your own herbes de provence ingredients - 0-1 tablespoon dried anise seed - 1-2 tablespoon dried lavender - 1-2 tablespoon dried basil - 1-2 tablespoon dried tarragon - 1 tablespoon fennel seeds - 0-1 teaspoon dried mint - 2 tablespoon to 1/4 cup dried thyme - 2-3 tablespoon dried marjoram - 1-2 tablespoon dried oregano - 1/2 to 2 tablespoon dried parsley and/or chervil - 2-3 tablespoon dried savory - 2 tablespoons dried rosemary - 1 teaspoon ground bay leaf powder instructions 1. combine all dried herbs and spices in a bowl or jar. 2. mix thoroughly until well blended. 3. store in an airtight container.

title: Slow Cooker Beef Bone Broth
text: slow cooker beef bone broth source: thehealthyfoodie.com ingredients - 3-4 lbs of mixed beef bones (oxtail, knuckles, neckbones and/or short ribs) - 2 medium carrots - 3 celery stalks - 2 medium onions - 2 tablespoons apple cider vinegar - 1 bay leaf - 10-12 cups water instructions 1. preheat oven to 400°f. 2. place the bones in a single layer on a baking sheet or roasting pan; roast for 60 minutes, flipping each bone over half way through cooking time. 3. place chopped vegetables (don't even bother peeling them), bay leaf, and vinegar in 7-quart slow cooker. add roasted bones and cover completely with water. 4. cook on low for 18-36 hours, until deep brown and aromatic. 5. carefully remove the larger pieces with a slotted spoon and place them in a colander set over a large bowl to collect the excess broth. then, strain the broth through a fine meshed sieve, or through a strainer that's been lined with cheesecloth. 6. transfer the bone broth into jars and refrigerate promptly. when cooled, remove fat layer and save it for cooking. 7. reheat before serving and season to taste.

title: Slow Cooker Beef Bone Broth
text: slow cooker beef bone broth source: the healthy foodie ingredients - 1.36 kg mixed beef bones, oxtail, knuckles, neckbones and/or short ribs - 2 medium carrots - 3 celery stalks - 2 medium onions - 2 tablespoons apple cider vinegar - 1 bay leaf - 2.5 kg water instructions 1. preheat your oven to 200°c. 2. place the bones in a single layer on a baking sheet or roasting pan and roast for 60 minutes, flipping each bone over halfway through cooking time. 3. roughly chop the vegetables without peeling them and place them along with the bay leaf and apple cider vinegar into a 6 quart slow cooker. 4. add the bones as soon as they come out of the oven and fill the pot completely with water. 5. set the slow cooker on low, cover and cook for 18 to 36 hours, or until the broth has reached a beautiful brown color. 6. carefully remove the larger pieces with a slotted spoon and place them in a strainer set over a large bowl to collect the excess broth. 7. strain the broth that's still in the crockpot through a fine meshed sieve or through a strainer lined with cheesecloth. 8. transfer the bone broth into jars and refrigerate promptly. 9. once the broth has fully cooled, remove some or all of the fat layer that formed at the top for use in cooking.

title: Mango Pickle Recipe
text: mango pickle recipe source: indianhealthyrecipes.com ingredients - 1 ¼ cup mango pieces (cubed (heaped cup, 1 medium mango)) - 1 tablespoon mustard seeds ( or 2 tbsp. mustard powder) - ½ teaspoon methi seeds ((fenugreek seeds)) - 3 tablespoon red chili powder ((use low heat spice powder, or adjust to taste)) - 1 ½ teaspoon salt (adjust as needed) - 4 garlic cloves (crushed) - 3 tablespoon oil instructions 1. choose raw, fresh and unripe green mango that is firm and has a clear skin. wash and dry mango thoroughly. wipe clean with a cloth. do this the previous night. 2. if possible sun dry the jar and other utensils used for making pickle, make sure all the bowls, spoons, chopping board and knife are dry. these precautions will increase the shelf life of the mango pickle. 3. dry roast methi seeds on a low flame until deep golden and aromatic. transfer to a plate and cool them completely. 4. to the same pan, pour oil and heat it up until slightly warm. set aside to cool completely. you can skip warming the oil if you intend to finish the mango pickle within 10 to 12 days. skip heating if using cold pressed oil. 5. blend methi seeds along with mustard seeds to a fine powder. crush garlic. 6. chop mangoes to slightly large cubes of 1 inch, using a large knife. 7. optional for shelf-life: sun dry each separately - spice powders, salt, garlic and chopped mangoes. alternately you may heat them in oven at 60 to 70 c (140 to 160f) for 1 hour (avoid keeping salt in oven) 8. add them to a dry bowl, along with red chili powder, mustard powder, salt and lightly crushed garlic. 9. pour the oil and mix well. the pickle will be dry at this stage. cover and set aside for 24 to 28 hours in a dry place. 10. after 24 to 28 hours, mango pieces will release juices and the consistency of the pickle will change. check the step-by-step photos above. stir mango pickle well and taste test it. if needed add more salt. 11. store this mango pickle in a clean dry glass jar. store it in the refrigerator after 24 hours. if storing at room temperature avoid storing in the kitchen or places with high moisture. 12. it will be ready to serve after 3 days but it tastes best as it ages. 13. use dry clean spoons every time you use. after every use, wipe off the sides of the jar with a clean tissue or dry cloth to avoid mold.

title: Marcella Hazan’s Legendary Tomato Sauce
text: marcella hazan’s legendary tomato sauce source: thekitchn.com ingredients - 1 (28-ounce) can whole tomatoes, no salt or herbs added - 5 tablespoons unsalted butter - 1 small white onion, peeled and cut in half - kosher salt - cooked pasta - finely grated parmesan cheese - freshly ground black pepper instructions 1. place 1 (28-ounce) can whole tomatoes, 5 tablespoons unsalted butter, 1 halved small white onion, and a pinch of kosher salt in a large saucepan and bring to a simmer over medium-high heat. 2. lower the heat to maintain a gentle simmer and cook, stirring and crushing the tomatoes lightly with the back of a spoon occasionally, until droplets of fat appear on the surface of the tomatoes, about 45 minutes. remove and discard the onion. 3. serve over hot pasta with grated parmesan cheese and ground black pepper if desired. 4. storage: leftovers can be refrigerated in an airtight container for up to 4 days or frozen for up to 3 months.adapted in my own words from marcella hazan's "essentials of classic italian cooking."

title: Mascarpone Mousse
text: mascarpone mousse source: food.com ingredients - 3/4 cup heavy whipping cream - 1 tablespoon granulated sugar - 4 ounces mascarpone cheese - 2 ounces cream cheese - 1/8 teaspoon pure vanilla extract - 3 tablespoons powdered sugar instructions 1. in a small chilled metal bowl whisk heavy cream in a figure eight motion. 2. just as soft peaks are forming, add the granulated sugar gradually. 3. continue whipping the cream until stiff peaks form. 4. cover the bowl and chill in an ice bath. 5. combine room temperature mascarpone and cream cheese with a rubber scraper. 6. add vanilla and powdered sugar. 7. when cheese mixture reaches a smooth consistency, set aside, keeping the mixture at room temperature. 8. just before serving, lightly fold whipped cream into the cheese mixture.

title: Mascarpone and Sweet Cream Ice Cream
text: mascarpone and sweet cream ice cream ingredients - 1 cup mascarpone cheese - 1 can (14 oz) sweetened condensed milk - 1 cup heavy cream - 1 tsp vanilla extract - a pinch of salt instructions 1. whip the heavy cream in a large bowl until soft peaks form. 2. in another bowl, whisk together the mascarpone cheese, sweetened condensed milk, vanilla extract, and a pinch of salt until smooth. 3. gently fold the whipped cream into the mascarpone mixture, making sure not to deflate the whipped cream too much. 4. pour the mixture into a container and cover with plastic wrap. 5. freeze for at least 4 hours or overnight. 6. once frozen, scoop and enjoy.

title: Meat 6
text: meat 6 ingredients - 3 tablespoons olive oil - 1 whole piece of meat - 1 onion, quartered - 2 whole carrots - 3 celery stalks - 1 celeriac, halved - 2 large pieces of parsley root - 1 bunch parsley, halved - 1 basket whole button mushrooms - 7 whole garlic cloves - 1 cup dry red wine - 2 bay leaves - 1 tablespoon coarse salt - 1/2 tablespoon ground black pepper - 1 cup water - a few leaves of sage instructions 1. in a pot, add three tablespoons of olive oil and sear the whole piece of meat on all sides until it gets a charred and perfect color. 2. add the quartered onion, whole carrots, celery stalks, halved celeriac, parsley root pieces, halved parsley, button mushrooms, garlic cloves, dry red wine, bay leaves, coarse salt, ground black pepper, water, and sage leaves to the pot. 3. cover the pot and transfer it to a turbo oven at 160 degrees for three hours. 4. serve with a side of pirto.

title: Aussie Meat Pie recipe
text: aussie meat pie recipe source: recipetineats.com ingredients - 1 1/2 batches homemade shortcrust pastry - 3 frozen shortcrust pastry sheets, thawed ((300g/10oz)) - 2 refrigerated pie crusts (us/can) - 3 frozen puff pastry sheets, just thawed ((300g/10oz) (note 2)) - 1 egg (, lightly whisked) - 1.25 kg / 2.5lb beef chuck (, 2.5cm/1" cubes (note 3)) - 1/2 tsp each salt & pepper - 2 - 3 tbsp olive oil - 1 onion (, diced) - 4 garlic cloves (, minced) - 5 tbsp flour (, plain/all purpose) - 1 1/4 cups (315 ml) beef stock, low sodium ((note 4)) - 3 cups (750 ml) red wine (, dry full bodied (note 5)) - 2 tbsp tomato paste - 1 tsp worcestershire sauce - 2 tsp black pepper (, coarsely ground) - 2 bay leaves instructions 1. sprinkle beef with 1/2 tsp salt and pepper. 2. heat 1 tbsp oil in a large heavy based pot over high heat. add 1/3 of the beef and brown aggressively all over, then remove. repeat with remaining beef, adding more oil if needed. 3. turn stove down to medium high. add garlic and onion, cook 3 minutes. 4. add flour, stir through. 5. slowly add beef stock while stirring constantly. once flour is dissolved, add wine, tomato paste, worcestershire, pepper and bay leaves. 6. return beef into pot, cover with lid, adjust heat so it's simmering gently. 7. simmer 1 hr 45 minutes. remove lid, increase heat slightly and simmer 30 - 45 minutes, stirring regularly, or until beef is fork tender and liquid reduces down to a thickish gravy, just about covering beef (see video). do not reduce liquid too much - thickens more as it cools & in pie. 8. remove from stove, cover and cool filling (i usually leave overnight). 9. preheat oven to 180c/350f. 10. cut out 6 rounds from the shortcrust pastry, then drape pastry into pie tins - don't stretch and pull pastry, causes shrinkage. (notes 1 & 6) 11. place pies on tray. top each pie with large sheets of parchment / baking paper and fill with pie weights (note 7). 12. bake 20 minutes, remove, then use paper overhang to carefully remove pie weights. 13. return crusts into oven for 5 minutes or until base is light golden and dry (can skip, note 8). remove from oven. 14. fill pies with cooled filling, push down to fill. should be slightly mounded. 15. cut rounds from partially thawed puff pastry - cut them slightly larger than the edge of the cooked pastry bases. 16. brush edge of pie crusts with egg, then place lid on filling, pressing edges to seal puff pastry to the shortcrust pastry. 17. brush lids with egg, then cut a 1cm / 0.5" incision in the middle using a small knife. 18. bake 30 minutes or until deep golden and puffed. 19. devour hot and fresh, topped with tomato sauce or ketchup if desired!

title: בורקס בשר ורוטב פטריות
text: בורקס בשר ורוטב פטריות source: crunchit.co.il ingredients - חבילה אחת בצק עלים או בצק פילאס - 500 גרם בשר טחון (צוואר או צלעות) - בצל גדול מאוד חתוך לקוביות קטנות - 2 שיני שום כתושות - 4 כפות שמן - רבע צרור פטרוזיליה קצוצה (רק העלים) - כף צנוברים קלויים - קופסת רסק עגבניות קטנה (100 גרם) - כף פפריקה מתוקה - כף שטוחה סוכר - כפית מלח - כפית פלפל גרוס - פפריקה חריפה (אופציונלי) - בצל חתוך לקוביות קטנות - סלסלת פטריות טריות או קופסת שימורים של פטריות חתוכות - 2 כוסות מים רותחים - 2 כפות קמח או קורנפלור - מלח לפי הטעם - פלפל שחור לפי הטעם - כף גדושה מרק עוף - ביצה למריחה - שומשום instructions 1. לשים שמן במחבת גדולה ועמוקה וטגן את הבצל עד שקיפות והזהבה קלה. 2. להוסיף את השום הכתוש ערבוב קצר ומיד להוסיף את הבשר הטחון. 3. לפרור את הבשר עם מזלג ולערבב כל הזמן עד שמחליף את הצבע. 4. להוסיף פלפל ומלח והעבירו לקערה. 5. באותה מחבת לשים כפית שמן ולהוסיף את הרסק, הפפריקה, הסוכר ומלח. 6. להוסיף את הבשר הטחון ולאחד בין התערובות. 7. להוסיף פטרוזיליה וצנוברים ולערבב להאחדת טעמים. 8. לטעום ולתקן תיבול ולהניח בצד להתקררות. 9. לטגן את הבצל עד שקיפות להכנת הרוטב. 10. להוסיף את הפטריות לאידוי נוזלים. 11. להוסיף מים וברזל כמה דקות תוך כדי ערבוב תמידי. 12. בכוס לשים 2 כפות קמח ולשפוך מים עליהם לערבב עד שאין גושים. 13. להכניס את תערובת הקמח לרוטב החם וערבב מהר עד איחוד. 14. להכניס מרק עוף ולהכביא את האש. 15. לחלק את בצק העלים לשניים ולפתוח מעט. 16. לשים בקצה כמות מהמילוי וגלגל לרולדה או לחתוך ריבועים ולמלא כל ריבוע. 17. למרוח על הבצק ביצה ולפזר שומשום. 18. להכניס לתנור שחומם מראש ל-180 מעלות עד שמזהיב (כ-45 דקות). 19. למזוג את הרוטב על הבורקס לפני הגשה.

title: Meatballs with Any Meat
text: meatballs with any meat ingredients - 1 pound ground meat (pork, beef, veal, chicken, turkey or a combination) - ½ cup panko bread crumbs - 1 egg - 1 teaspoon kosher salt, more as needed - black pepper and/or ground cumin, curry powder, chile flakes, garam masala, etc., to taste - minced garlic, onion, scallions or shallot - chopped parsley, basil or cilantro - olive oil, for frying (optional) instructions 1. in a large bowl, gently combine all ingredients, roll into 1½-inch balls, and transfer to a baking sheet. 2. broil until golden and firm for 7 to 10 minutes, or fry in oil until deeply browned all over. 3. sprinkle with more salt before serving.

title: Mozzarella
text: mozzarella ingredients - 1¼ cups water, divided - 1½ tsp citric acid - ¼ rennet tablet - 1 gallon whole milk or 2% milk (not ultra-pasteurized/uht) - 1 tsp kosher salt instructions 1. dissolve citric acid in 1 cup cold water and dissolve rennet in ¼ cup cold water, then set aside. 2. pour milk into a large pot, add citric acid solution and stir well, then heat over medium heat to 90°f (32°c) while stirring gently. 3. remove from heat, add the rennet solution and stir gently for 30 seconds, then cover and let sit for 5 minutes undisturbed. 4. check the curd to ensure it looks like soft tofu, letting it sit another 5 minutes if too soft, then cut the curd into ½-inch cubes with a knife. 5. return pot to medium heat, heat curds to 105°f (40°c) while gently stirring, then remove from heat and continue stirring slowly for 2–3 minutes. 6. scoop the curds into a microwave-safe bowl using a slotted spoon, draining off as much whey as possible and reserving the whey. 7. microwave curds on high for 1 minute, drain off excess whey, and fold curds over themselves several times. 8. microwave again for 30 seconds, drain whey and fold again, then repeat once more until the cheese reaches 135°f (57°c) and is smooth and stretchy. 9. add salt and knead it into the cheese. 10. stretch and fold the cheese until smooth and glossy, like taffy. 11. form into a ball or desired shape, then place in cool water or salted whey to firm up, and use immediately or refrigerate.

title: Mushroom Potpie
text: mushroom potpie source: new york times cooking ingredients - ½ cup dried porcini mushrooms (1/2 ounce) - 4 tablespoons olive oil, plus more as needed - ½ pound fresh oyster mushrooms, torn into separate pieces (or shiitake mushrooms, stemmed and halved) - kosher salt and black pepper - ½ pound cremini mushrooms, stemmed and quartered (or cut into sixths if large) - 4 tablespoons unsalted butter - 1 large yellow onion, finely chopped - ¼ pound lacinato kale, stemmed, leaves thinly sliced crosswise - 4 garlic cloves, chopped - 1 tablespoon fresh thyme leaves - 2 teaspoons chopped fresh rosemary - ¼ cup all-purpose flour, plus more for dusting - 1½ cups chicken or vegetable stock - ¾ cup heavy cream - 1 cup diced peeled carrots (from 2 medium carrots, cut into 1/2-inch pieces) - 1 cup diced peeled parsnips (from 2 medium parsnips, cut into 1/2-inch pieces) - 1 cup diced red potatoes (from 2 small potatoes, cut into 1/2-inch pieces) - 1 (14- to 16-ounce) package puff pastry, thawed - 1 large egg instructions 1. heat oven to 425 degrees and bring 2 cups of water to boil in a small pot. 2. place the porcini mushrooms in a medium bowl and pour the boiling water on top; set aside to soak and soften. 3. in a large (12-inch) ovenproof skillet, heat 2 tablespoons oil over medium-high and working in two batches, add half the oyster mushrooms, season with salt and pepper and cook undisturbed until browned underneath, about 3 minutes. 4. stir the oyster mushrooms and continue to cook until browned all over, about 3 minutes, then transfer to a medium bowl. 5. repeat with 2 tablespoons oil and the remaining oyster mushrooms and transfer them to the medium bowl. 6. add another 2 tablespoons oil, then add the cremini mushrooms, season with salt and pepper and cook, stirring occasionally, until browned and tender, 6 to 8 minutes, lowering the heat as needed to avoid burning, then transfer to the bowl. 7. reduce the heat to medium and add the butter to the skillet, then once melted, add the onion and cook until starting to soften, about 5 minutes. 8. add the kale, garlic, thyme and rosemary, season with salt and pepper and cook, stirring occasionally, until softened, about 3 minutes, adding 1 to 2 tablespoons oil if the pan seems dry. 9. sprinkle with the flour and cook, stirring, until flour is dispersed and lightly toasted, 2 minutes. 10. stirring constantly, gradually add the stock, cream and 3/4 cup of the liquid from the soaking porcini mushrooms. 11. cook over medium heat, stirring occasionally, until thickened, about 5 minutes, then remove from heat. 12. stir in the carrots, parsnips, potatoes, and the sautéed mushrooms and any accumulated juices. 13. strain the soaked porcini mushrooms, discard any remaining liquid, then roughly chop the mushrooms and stir them into the filling. 14. season to taste with salt and pepper. 15. on a lightly dusted work surface using a lightly floured rolling pin, roll out the puff pastry into a roughly 14-inch circle. 16. transfer the puff pastry to the top of the skillet, allowing slight overhang, and fold under and pinch any overhang just below the rim of the skillet. 17. in a small bowl, whisk the egg with 1 teaspoon water and lightly brush the egg wash over the top of the puff pastry. 18. cut 5 (2-inch) slits into the puff pastry, starting near the center and radiating outward like the rays of the sun, or create a stripe or crisscross pattern by gently scoring it with a paring knife without fully cutting through. 19. crimp the edges using the tines of a fork if desired. 20. set the skillet on top of an aluminum foil-lined baking sheet and transfer to the middle rack of the oven. 21. bake until the puff pastry is puffed and golden, about 30 minutes, then let sit 10 minutes before serving.

title: Napoleon (Cream Cake)
text: napoleon (cream cake) source: domowe-wypieki.pl ingredients - 300 g butter - 300 g wheat flour - 1 egg (size m) - 1/2 tablespoon vinegar (about 5%) - approximately 100 ml hot water - 1 liter milk - 50 g butter - 4 egg yolks - 2 eggs (size m) - 200 g sugar - 2 teaspoons vanilla sugar - 120 g wheat flour - 70 g potato starch - powdered sugar for sprinkling instructions 1. prepare puff pastry by kneading 300 g butter and 100 g flour to a homogeneous mass, then place it between two pieces of food foil and flatten it by hand or roll out into a square about 2 cm thick, and refrigerate. 2. during this time, knead the dough from the remaining ingredients with enough water to make it resemble pierogi dough, then roll it out on a flour-covered surface into a circle. 3. place the cooled butter mass from the fridge in the center of the rolled dough, fold the dough into an envelope, and glue the edges thoroughly. 4. invert the dough with the joints facing downwards and roll out into a long rectangle approximately 1 cm thick, always rolling in one direction. 5. fold the dough into three parts like a letter, lightly roll out just by pressing with a roller to make it thinner, wrap in foil, and place on a wooden board in the freezer for 15 minutes. 6. remove the dough from the freezer, turn it 90 degrees, and roll it out again into an oblong rectangle, then re-fold as a letter, lightly roll out, wrap in foil, and place in the freezer for 15 minutes. 7. repeat the folding and freezing process two more times, each time placing the dough in the freezer for 15 minutes. 8. cut the finished dough in half, wrap one half in foil, and refrigerate. 9. roll out the other half of the dough on a flour-covered countertop into a large rectangular cake, transfer it to a large flat oven tray lined with baking paper, trim the edges with a knife, and prick with a fork. 10. bake in a preheated oven at 220°c with the top-down heater for about 15 minutes until golden brown, opening the oven after a few minutes to prick any bulges with a fork. 11. bake the second cake in the same way and allow both cakes to cool completely. 12. cut one cake intended for the top with a serrated knife into squares of the desired size for individual portions. 13. prepare the pudding mass by boiling approximately 750 ml of milk with butter, sugar, and vanilla sugar, then mix the remaining milk with eggs, yolks, flour, and starch and add to the boiling milk while stirring to prevent lumps from forming, and cook until thick. 14. allow the pudding to cool slightly while stirring briefly every now and then, then pour it still slightly warm onto the first puff pastry cake, wrapping the bottom with aluminum foil rolled several times to prevent the pudding from flowing out. 15. arrange the cut squares on top of the pudding mass. 16. place the cake in the refrigerator for at least a few hours. 17. sprinkle with powdered sugar and cut with a sharp serrated knife.

title: Naturally Leavened Bomboloni (Doughnuts)
text: naturally leavened bomboloni (doughnuts) source: theperfectloaf.com ingredients - 45g mature 100% hydration starter - 90g all-purpose white flour - 90g water - 253g all-purpose white flour - 253g high-protein bread flour - 187g eggs (about 3 large plus 1 yolk, cold) - 101g unsalted european butter - 101g fine white sugar - 91g water - 10g salt - 203g mature 100% hydration levain - 2g ground cinnamon - 200g sugar - 365g whole milk - 30g all-purpose flour - 100g fine sugar - 4 large egg yolks - 1g salt - 4g vanilla extract - zest of 1 lemon (optional) instructions 1. build levain with 45g mature starter, 90g all-purpose flour, and 90g water in the morning. store at 78°f until ripe, approximately 5 hours. 2. soften butter and cut into half-inch cubes. bring eggs to weight and keep cold. 3. add flour, sugar, eggs, levain, salt, and water to mixer with paddle attachment. stir 1 minute, then mix on speed two for 5 minutes and rest 10 minutes. 4. mix on speed three for 9-10 minutes, adding butter chunk by chunk, until dough almost passes the windowpane test. 5. perform 4 sets of stretch and folds every 30 minutes over 2 hours. rest for 4 hours after final fold, aiming for at least 30% rise. cover and refrigerate overnight. 6. allow flexible cold fermentation overnight. 7. dump cold dough on unfloured surface and divide into 18 pieces of 65g each. preshape into tight rounds with taut surface. 8. place on floured trays, 8 per tray. proof at 78°f for approximately 12 hours until nearly doubled and very puffy. bomboloni should feel air-filled when poked. 9. heat oil to 360-370°f in a heavy pot. fry bomboloni smooth-side down first, up to 3 at a time, for 2.5 minutes per side until golden brown. 10. drain fried bomboloni, then toss in cinnamon-sugar mixture while warm. 11. for crema pasticcera, heat milk until bubbles form on sides. whisk together flour, salt, and sugar, then add egg yolks to form a thick paste. 12. slowly pour warm milk over yolk mixture while whisking constantly. return to pot on medium heat and whisk until large bubbles pop. 13. strain crema through fine mesh. stir in vanilla extract and lemon zest if desired. 14. cover with plastic wrap on surface and refrigerate until firm. pipe into bomboloni just before serving.

title: New York Style Sourdough Bagels
text: new york style sourdough bagels source: baked-theblog.com ingredients - 1 cup active sourdough starter - 1 1/4 cups cold water - 2 tablespoons barley malt syrup (or maple syrup) - 5 cups all-purpose flour - 2 teaspoons fine salt - flour (or semolina for proofing) - 1 tablespoon baking soda - 1 tablespoon brown sugar - 1/2 cup any combination of poppy seeds/dried onion flakes/dried garlic flakes/sesame seeds/flaky salt/za'atar instructions 1. in the bowl of a stand mixer fitted with a paddle attachment, mix your bubbly, active starter with the water and maple syrup until well-combined. alternatively, mix in a standard large bowl with a fork or whisk. 2. add in the flour and salt and transition to a dough hook. knead on medium until the dough is smooth and somewhat pliable, about 6-7 minutes. alternatively, knead the dough by hand on a countertop until smooth and pliable. 3. shape into a ball (return to bowl, if applicable) and cover bowl with a towel. rest 20 minutes. 4. divide the dough into 8 equal pieces for large bagels or 10 equal pieces for smaller ones. shape each piece into a small ball by tucking the corners underneath, cupping the dough, and rolling it in a circular fashion on a clean, flour-free countertop. this helps to create surface tension and a skin on the ball. 5. cover dough balls and rest another 15 minutes. 6. line a baking sheet with parchment paper and sprinkle generously with flour or semolina. note: if you make 10 bagels, you will need to use 2 baking sheets. 7. flatten the ball of dough into a disc and use your fingertips to roll into a log about 8 inches (20 cm) long. 8. wrap the log around your three middle fingers with the ends overlapping by 2 inches (5 cm) on the inside of your hand. 9. roll gently, palm down, until the ends are joined together. this will create a larger hole in the centre of the bagel. 10. poke a hole with your finger directly through the centre of the dough ball. 11. insert both index fingers into the hole and roll fingers around each other to stretch out the centre (like a barrel roll) until it’s about the size of a walnut. this will create a smaller bagel hole, but is much faster and more efficient to do. 12. place on the lined baking sheet and repeat with the rest of the bagels. this is a fun step to do with kids 3 years old or older. 13. cover the shaped bagels with a towel, let them proof at room temperature for 2.5 to 4.5 hours, or until puffy. this could take more time, depending on the temperature in your house. 14. take a test bagel and place it in cold water. if it floats, they’re done proofing. dry the test bagel off and return to the baking sheet. if it sinks, it still needs to proof longer. 15. once proofed, cover the pan with plastic wrap and refrigerate 12 to 24 hours. 16. preheat oven to 450°f (230°c). place toppings on flat plates, so they are ready to go. 17. bring a large pot of water to a rolling boil and add the baking soda and brown sugar. 18. remove the bagels from the fridge and gently place them, a couple at a time, into the water. 19. boil for 15 to 20 seconds on each side. 20. remove boiled bagels with a slotted spoon to get rid of most of the water. 21. shake off excess water and immediately dip the top of bagel into desired toppings. 22. set back on the baking sheet. 23. repeat this process with the remaining bagels. 24. place the baking sheet into the center of the oven and turn it down to 400°f (200°c). 25. bake for 18 to 22 minutes or until golden on top. 26. cool on a wire rack until ready to serve.

title: New York Style Sourdough Bagels
text: new york style sourdough bagels source: baked ingredients - 1 cup active sourdough starter - 1 ¼ cups cold water - 2 tablespoons barley malt syrup or maple syrup - 5 cups all-purpose flour - 2 teaspoons fine salt - flour or semolina for proofing - 1 tablespoon baking soda - 1 tablespoon brown sugar - ½ cup toppings (poppy seeds, dried onion flakes, dried garlic flakes, sesame seeds, flaky salt, or za'atar) instructions 1. in a stand mixer bowl fitted with a paddle attachment, mix the active starter with water and maple syrup until well combined. 2. add the flour and salt and switch to a dough hook, kneading on medium until the dough is smooth and pliable, about 6-7 minutes. 3. shape the dough into a ball, cover with a towel, and rest for 20 minutes. 4. divide the dough into 8 pieces for large bagels or 10 pieces for smaller ones, shaping each into a ball with surface tension. 5. cover the dough balls and rest for another 15 minutes. 6. line a baking sheet with parchment paper and sprinkle generously with flour or semolina. 7. cover the shaped bagels with a towel and let them proof at room temperature for 2.5 to 4.5 hours until puffy, or perform a float test in cold water to check readiness. 8. once proofed, cover with plastic wrap and refrigerate for 12 to 24 hours. 9. preheat the oven to 450°f and place toppings on flat plates. 10. bring a large pot of water to a rolling boil and add the baking soda and brown sugar. 11. gently place the bagels a couple at a time into the boiling water and boil for 15 to 20 seconds on each side. 12. remove boiled bagels with a slotted spoon and immediately dip the top into desired toppings. 13. return the bagels to the baking sheet and repeat with the remaining bagels. 14. place the baking sheet in the center of the oven and reduce temperature to 400°f, then bake for 18 to 22 minutes until golden on top. 15. cool on a wire rack until ready to serve.

title: Ninja Grilled Salmon
text: ninja grilled salmon source: girlscangrill.com ingredients - 3 lb salmon filet - 1/4 cup olive oil - 1 tbsp kosher salt - 1 tbsp brown sugar - 2 tsp coarse ground black pepper - 1/2 tsp granulated garlic - 1/4 tsp ground ginger - 1/8 tsp ground cayenne pepper instructions 1. combine all of the rub ingredients in a small bowl. 2. cut the salmon in half so it will fit on the ninja grill. 3. brush both sides with olive oil. 4. sprinkle both sides with rub. 5. set the ninja grill to the grill function, set the heat to high and the time to 20 minutes. 6. place the filets on the grill skin side up and grill for 5-6 minutes. 7. flip the salmon and grill for 8-10 minutes to an internal temperature of 62 degrees celsius. 8. remove from the grill and serve.

title: Ninja Woodfire Grill Smoky Whole Chicken
text: ninja woodfire grill smoky whole chicken source: grillwhatyoulove.com ingredients - 1 whole chicken, 3-4 pounds - 2 tablespoons montreal chicken seasoning or your favorite chicken rub - wood pellets (apple, cherry, or pecan recommended) instructions 1. preheat your ninja woodfire outdoor grill to the grill setting on high heat. 2. add pellets to the hopper and press the woodfire button to add smoke. 3. set the cook time for 35 to 40 minutes. 4. spatchcock the chicken by placing it breast side down, cutting along both sides of the backbone with kitchen shears, removing the backbone, and pressing the chicken flat. 5. pat the chicken skin completely dry with paper towels. 6. sprinkle both sides generously with montreal chicken seasoning. 7. place the chicken on the grill skin-side down and cook for 5 to 6 minutes to sear the skin. 8. flip the chicken over and reduce the heat to low. 9. continue cooking the chicken cut-side down for 15 to 20 minutes. 10. flip the chicken back to skin-side down and continue cooking until the internal temperature reaches 160°f. 11. remove the chicken from the grill and let it rest for a few minutes so the juices can redistribute. 12. carve and serve.

title: No Bake Cheesecake With Condensed Milk
text: no bake cheesecake with condensed milk source: cookingwithcarlee.com ingredients - graham cracker crust - 16 oz. cream cheese (softened) - 14 oz. sweetened condensed milk - ⅓ cup sour cream - 2 teaspoons lemon juice (optional) instructions 1. in a medium bowl, mix 16 oz. cream cheese on low speed until it is creamy and lump free. be sure to scrape the sides of the bowl and the beater a few times along the way. 2. slowly add the 14 oz. sweetened condensed milk, mixing on low after each addition until it is incorporated fully. 3. mix in ⅓ cup sour cream until incorporated. if using 2 teaspoons lemon juice, add now. 4. spoon the cream cheese mixture into the prepared graham cracker crust. 5. chill for at least 4 hours, though longer is better, before serving.

title: Nougat
text: nougat ingredients - 1 cup granulated sugar - 1/2 cup honey - 2 egg whites - 1 cup nuts (such as almonds, hazelnuts, or pistachios), coarsely chopped - 1 tsp vanilla extract instructions 1. in a small saucepan, combine the sugar and honey and cook over medium heat, stirring constantly, until the sugar has dissolved and the mixture has reached a temperature of 240°f on a candy thermometer. 2. beat the egg whites in a large mixing bowl until stiff peaks form. 3. when the sugar mixture has reached the correct temperature, carefully pour it into the egg whites in a thin stream while continuing to beat the mixture on high speed. 4. add the vanilla extract and nuts to the mixture and continue beating until the mixture is thick and glossy. 5. spread the mixture evenly into a greased 8x8-inch baking dish and let the nougat cool completely before cutting it into squares. 6. serve the nougat as is, or use it as a filling for chocolate bars or other sweets.

title: Oatmeal Creme Pies
text: oatmeal creme pies ingredients - 1 1/4 cups room temperature butter - 1 cup packed dark brown sugar - 1/2 cup granulated sugar - 1 large egg - 2 teaspoons vanilla extract - 1 tablespoon dark molasses - 1 1/2 cups all purpose flour - 1 teaspoon baking soda - 1/2 teaspoon salt - 3/4 teaspoon cinnamon - 1/4 teaspoon ground cloves, nutmeg, or pumpkin spice - 3 cups quick cooking oats - 3/4 cup room temperature butter (for filling) - 3 cups sifted confectionery sugar - 1 1/2 teaspoons vanilla extract (for filling) - up to 3 tablespoons heavy cream - salt to taste instructions 1. bring the butter to room temperature, or place it in a warm location to soften if you forgot to do so overnight. 2. in one bowl, cream together the 1 1/4 cups room temperature butter, 1 cup packed dark brown sugar, and 1/2 cup granulated sugar. 3. whip for about a minute and a half until the mixture becomes fluffy and lighter in color. 4. add one large egg, two teaspoons vanilla extract, and 1 tablespoon dark molasses to the butter mixture. 5. in another bowl, sift together 1 1/2 cups all purpose flour, 1 teaspoon baking soda, 1/2 teaspoon salt, 3/4 teaspoon cinnamon, and 1/4 teaspoon ground cloves, nutmeg, or pumpkin spice. 6. add 3 cups quick cooking oats to the dry ingredients and whisk to combine. 7. add the dry ingredients to the wet ingredients a little at a time, mixing by hand and lightly folding until just combined without overworking the dough. 8. form equal 3 ounce balls of dough. 9. bake at 375 degrees for 11 minutes. 10. remove from the oven and leave the cookies on the baking sheet for 3 minutes before transferring to a cooling rack. 11. for the filling, combine 3/4 cups room temperature butter and 3 cups of sifted confectionery sugar in a bowl and mix. 12. add 1 1/2 teaspoons vanilla extract and mix. 13. add up to 3 tablespoons heavy cream to reach your preferred consistency. 14. whip the filling for 4 minutes until fluffy. 15. add salt to taste, about a pinch or two. 16. once the cookies are cooled, assemble them into sandwiches with the filling.

title: עוגיות שיבולת שועל
text: עוגיות שיבולת שועל מצרכים - 1 כוס קמח - 3/4 כפית אבקת אפייה - 1/2 כפית סודה לשתיה - 200 גרם חמאה - 1 כוס סוכר - 1/4 כוס סוכר חום בהיר - 1 ביצה גדולה - 1 כפית תמצית וניל - 2.5 כוסות שיבולת שועל (לא מיידית) הוראות 1. מחממים תנור ל-180 מעלות צלזיוס ומכינים 3 גליונות אפייה מרופדים בנייר אפייה. 2. טורפים יחד את הקמח, אבקת האפייה, הסודה והמלח. 3. מקציפים עם המיקסר במהירות נמוכה את החמאה והסוכר עד שגרגרי הסוכר אינם גלויים. 4. מגבירים את מהירות המיקסר ומכים עוד דקה, גורדים את צדי הקערה, מוסיפים ביצה ומכים עוד 30 שניות. 5. מוסיפים את הקמח לתערובת בשלישים ומערבבים היטב בכל פעם עד לקבלת תערובת חלקה. 6. מוסיפים את שיבולת השועל ומערבבים לתוך הבצק בעזרת כף. 7. מחלקים את הבצק ל-24 חלקים שווים ומניחים על נייר אפייה. 8. אופים ל-13-16 דקות, מסובבים את נייר האפייה באמצע הבישול.

title: Old Fashioned Potato Knishes – Kosher From Jerusalem
text: old fashioned potato knishes – kosher from jerusalem <https://kosherfromjerusalem.com/2020/12/14/old-fashioned-potato-knishes/ --- [](https://kosherfromjerusalem.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/12/img1628-min.jpg "old fashioned potato knishes") growing up in new york, there were certain foods that you associated with your city. knishes were unquestionably one of them. my late father was a huge fan of kasha and potato knishes and my brother avi to this day loves them. the big shocker is that when i made these (a bunch of times, natch) my mom (!) of all people, said, this should become a regular in your repertoire. frankly, i’m still reeling from the shock. but it gives you an idea of how well these went over. don’t worry, i sent some to avi as well. so i checked out many many recipes for knish dough and was disappointed time and again (cookbooks, online etc.) until lo and behold, i spotted a recipe recommended by deb from smitten kitchen and decided to go to the original guy who crafted it. his name is joe and his website is called joe pastry and the guy is awesome. not only do i love his website but he is personable and professional. he also wrote me back and is very encouraging. way to go joe! (sorry, i couldn’t help myself 🙂 ). and so, i finally have an awesome knish recipe. this dough is actually ridiculously easy to make, no yeast, no worries, and all you need is the patience of letting it rest for an hour. yes, yep, nothing to be done about that, ya gotta do it. if you don’t let it rest, the dough will just not be properly workable but if you do (you are relaxing the gluten in the dough), promise! it’s a pleasure. adult playdough if you get me. so you should start with the dough since you need that resting time. it’s done in a bowl, no mixer or processor needed. take your flour, baking powder and salt and whisk briefly in a medium bowl, preferably one with a lid. whisking dry ingredients together then make a well (sorta a little crater in the middle of the flour mixture) and put the egg, oil, water and vinegar in it, and mix it all up till incorporated. mixing wet ingredients with dry stir it up till it looks like so: knish dough if there’s a bit of flour on the bottom of your bowl, no worries, since right in the bowl, using your hands, you should knead the dough about 6 times, (fold and press, 1/4 turn and again) and then take the lid and close it. otherwise, take some plastic wrap and cover. dough resting in bowl with lid set aside (you might want to time it to be sure, 1 hour, no cheating). a note, it might “weep” a little oil. no worries, just stir back in. now if you’ve been doing the sauteeing of onions and storing the extras in your fridge or freezer as i recommend basic sauteed onions, a kitchen staple, you’ve saved a step. otherwise, you need to sautee an onion. no big, do so and on to your potato filling. peel about 5 medium potatoes and chunk or cube them (the faster to cook them, m’dear) put in a pot with salt, cover with boiling water and cook on medium simmer till really truly soft. we are gonna mash ’em. into a bowl and whip out your potato masher (or a fork if you ain’t got one). a note. do not, no no no put potatoes into a food processor or blender. they get a gummy texture and are just gross. mashing will go fast if they are really soft (check with a toothpick to be sure). mashing those suckers next add your sauteed onions and salt and this may seem odd but is not, beat a large egg and put 1/2 (yes, half) the egg into the mixture. you are saving the other half to brush on top of the knish when ready. mix it all about. mixing the potato filling see the other half of the egg? yup for real. okay. your filling is ready to roll, and yuk yuk, so is your dough so now preheat your oven to 350 f. now take the rested dough and divide into four pieces, covering the ones you aren’t working with, sprinkle some flour on parchment paper, take a rolling pin and roll into a rectangle. the dough is soft and will roll nice and thin. roll dough into rectangle now scoop up a quarter of your potato filling and place in a line on the bottom of the dough nearest you. leave a bit of a margin. like so: place filling on dough brush the flour away and roll the first bit of dough over the filling and then, using the parchment paper, lift it up a bit and the dough should just roll over and over covering the filling a number of times. if it doesn’t work for you, just gently roll it up yourself with your hands. your dough should look like this: rolling the dough and then this: dough log now take the dough and sort of pat the filling so it is even and with your fingers, pinch the dough evenly so it looks like this: pinching the dough i didn’t want mammoth size knishes so this was perfect for me. as you wish. next twist the end piece of dough/knish to sort of tie it off from its mates. twisted dough after twisting, cut with a sharp knife to separate. then stand them up on their little bottoms and gently press down and push your index finger lightly into the middle. presto, you’ve made a knish. with a little practice you will become an expert. do this with all the dough (you might have a little filling left over, serve beef or chicken on it, don’t let it go to waste!) and put on parchment lined rimmed baking sheet. remember the 1/2 an egg? now use it and brush the knishes to glaze them. this makes them brown nicely in the oven. bake in the hot oven 30-40 minutes or till golden brown. serve with brown mustard and astound your family! click here to print recipe old fashioned potato knishes dough: 2 cups (312 grams) all-purpose flour 1 tsp baking powder 1 tsp salt 1 large egg 1/2 cup canola oil 1/2 cup lukewarm water 1 tsp vinegar filling: 5 medium potatoes, peeled and cut into chunks boiling water to cover pinch of salt one medium onion, peeled and chopped 2 tablespoons oil 1 large egg 1 teaspoon salt extra flour to sprinkle on parchment paper or silpat ingredients instructions preheat the oven to 350 f/180 c. in a medium bowl (best if it has its own cover, otherwise you will need plastic wrap), whisk together your dry ingredients, make a well in the center of the flour mixture and add the egg, oil, vinegar and water. stir together till all the ingredients are incorporated and then right in the bowl, knead the dough about six times, just pressing and turning to make sure all the ingredients have been properly mixed. cover the bowl with the lid or plastic wrap and let the dough sit for an hour at room temperature. set aside. prepare the filling by boiling the potatoes with the pinch of salt till very soft. put potatoes in a bowl to cool. sautee the onions in the oil till medium brown and add to the potatoes and mash together and add a teaspoon of salt. stir well. when filling is cool, beat the egg and pour half the egg into the potato mixture saving the other half to brush on the finished knishes. divide the rested dough into 4 parts. roll out the dough on a floured piece of parchment paper into a rectangle and along the bottom of the dough (short side) leaving a bit of a margin, place a layer of potato filling. encase the filling with one turn of dough and then using the parchment paper, lift up the edge and gently roll and the dough should fold over itself like a jelly roll. pinch the dough at intervals (i did 4-5 knishes from a rectangle of dough) and twist. cut at the twist, pinch the ends shut and sit on their bottoms, gently poking the top to help seal and make a small indentation. place on parchment paper on rimmed baking sheet, brush with the remaining egg mixture, and do this with the rest of dough and filling. if you have filling left over, serve as a side dish. bake the knishes 30-40 minutes or till golden brown. serve with mustard, of course 🙂 . a note, these reheat beautifully and will keep (ha! try it and see how long they last) at least 5 days in the fridge. <https://joepastry.com/2009/thetradishknish/ ! title: Onion Rings
text: onion rings ingredients - 4 large white onions - 700 ml milk - 2 eggs - 1 tablespoon dijon mustard - 500 grams all-purpose flour - 1 level tablespoon salt - 1 tablespoon smoked paprika - 1 tablespoon garlic powder - 1 tablespoon baking powder - panko breadcrumbs - breadcrumbs - oil for frying (170°c) instructions 1. cut four large white onions into thick rings and carefully separate them so they don't break. 2. in a large bowl, combine 500 grams flour, salt, smoked paprika, garlic powder, and baking powder and mix well. 3. in a separate bowl, whisk together 700 ml milk, dijon mustard, and 2 eggs. 4. add the flour mixture to the wet ingredients and mix thoroughly. 5. heat oil to 170°c. 6. dip each onion ring in plain flour, then dip in the batter, and then coat with panko breadcrumbs mixed with breadcrumbs. 7. fry the coated rings in hot oil for approximately 1 minute on each side until golden brown.

title: Overnight Baked Blueberry Muffin Oatmeal
text: overnight baked blueberry muffin oatmeal source: abeautifulmess.com ingredients - 1¾ cups old-fashioned oats - ¼ cup sugar - 1 teaspoon baking powder - ⅛ teaspoon salt - 1½ cups milk - 1 egg - 2 tablespoons melted and cooled butter - 1 teaspoon vanilla extract - 1 cup blueberries - ¼ cup cold butter - ¼ cup sugar - ¼ cup all-purpose flour instructions 1. in a large bowl, stir together the oats, sugar, baking powder, and salt. 2. in a smaller bowl, stir together the milk, egg, melted and cooled butter, and vanilla extract. 3. combine the wet ingredients with the dry in the large bowl and stir to combine, then stir in the blueberries. 4. add this mixture to a pie pan, cover and store overnight in the refrigerator. 5. in a small bowl, cut together the crumb topping ingredients until the mixture is crumbly like small peas you can press together, then store overnight or make in the morning. 6. top the oatmeal with the crumb topping and bake at 350°f for 30-35 minutes, or set under the broiler for a minute or two if the crumb topping doesn't look golden brown and slightly crispy.

title: Overnight Waffle
text: overnight waffle ingredients - 2 cups all-purpose flour - 1 cup sourdough starter (unfed/discard) - 2 tbsp sugar - 2 cups buttermilk - 2 large eggs - ¼ cup vegetable oil or 4 tbsp melted butter - ¾ tsp salt - 1 tsp baking soda instructions 1. the night before, combine flour, sourdough starter, sugar, and buttermilk in a large bowl and stir until smooth. 2. cover the bowl loosely and let rest at room temperature overnight for 8–12 hours. 3. in the morning, whisk together eggs, oil or butter, salt, and baking soda in a small bowl. 4. add the egg mixture to the sponge and stir gently until just combined. 5. for waffles, pour batter into a preheated, greased waffle iron and cook according to manufacturer's instructions until golden and crisp. 6. serve immediately and keep finished waffles warm in a 200°f oven while cooking remaining batches.

title: Pickled Artichokes
text: pickled artichokes ingredients - 4 lemons (juice used for prep and brine) - 1 cup white vinegar - ½ cup olive oil - 4 garlic cloves, thinly sliced - 2 dried chiles - a dozen juniper berries (optional) - 1 bay leaf - 2 tsp sea salt - 25 baby artichokes instructions 1. prepare an acidulated water bath by filling a large bowl with cold water, squeezing in the juice of 2 lemons, and dropping in the squeezed lemon halves. 2. trim the baby artichokes by removing the tough outer leaves, cutting off the top third, trimming the stem, and halving or quartering them, then immediately drop into the lemon water to prevent browning. 3. make the brine by combining vinegar, olive oil, juice of remaining 2 lemons, garlic, dried chiles, juniper berries, bay leaf, and sea salt in a large saucepan and bringing to a boil. 4. drain the artichokes and add to the boiling brine, then cook for 5–7 minutes until just tender but not mushy. 5. pack artichokes into sterilized mason jars, ladle brine over them, and seal, then process in a water bath for 15 minutes for shelf-stable storage or refrigerate immediately.

title: Homemade Paneer
text: homemade paneer ingredients - full fat milk - lemon juice or vinegar - cheesecloth instructions 1. heat milk to 80–85 degrees celsius using a food thermometer, being careful not to let it boil or overflow. 2. add lemon juice or vinegar one teaspoon at a time, stirring for a minute between each addition. 3. use a maximum of 2 tablespoons of lemon juice or vinegar per liter of milk. 4. stop adding the acidic agent once the milk has started curdling well. 5. pour the curdled milk through cheesecloth to strain. 6. place the curds in cheesecloth and apply approximately 10 kg of weight on top to press the paneer.

title: Pastila
text: pastila source: atlas obscura ingredients - 6 large apples (granny smith if antonovka unavailable) - ¾ cup granulated sugar - 2 egg whites - powdered sugar for dusting instructions 1. preheat your oven to 350°f, wash the apples, place them in a shallow oven-safe dish with ¼ inch of water at the bottom, and roast for an hour until golden, saggy, and wrinkly. 2. remove the apples from the oven and allow them to cool completely, then scrape the skins and cores to create soft, seed-free puree and process in a blender until smooth. 3. put the puree, egg whites, and granulated sugar in a stand mixer bowl and whip for 10 minutes, scraping down the sides occasionally. 4. preheat the oven to 180°f or the lowest setting and line a cookie sheet with parchment paper. 5. stop the mixer once the puree has nearly quadrupled in size and formed a thick white foam, then scrape the foam into the pan, reserving about a cup and a half in the fridge. 6. spread the remaining foam in the pan evenly and leave it in the oven for 4 to 6 hours until it is dry to the touch and solid enough to pick up as one sheet without being extremely floppy. 7. remove the pastila from the oven and allow it to cool completely before peeling away the parchment paper. 8. with a knife dipped in hot water, cut the pastila into three identical rectangles and use the reserved puree as glue to stack the three pieces on top of each other, patching any holes or pits. 9. return the stacked pastila to the oven on a parchment-lined baking sheet for an hour and a half until the layers have molded together, then remove and allow to cool. 10. rub the cooled pastila all over with powdered sugar and carefully slice through the layers in inch-long increments, then store in a sealed container.

title: Pecan Pie Cheesecake
text: pecan pie cheesecake source: bakedbyanintrovert.com ingredients for the crust - 2 cups graham cracker crumbs, about 18 whole crackers - 1 cup pecans, finely ground - ¼ cup light brown sugar, packed - ½ cup unsalted butter, melted for the filling - 16 ounces cream cheese, softened - ½ cup granulated sugar - ½ cup sour cream, room temperature - 1 tablespoon vanilla extract - ¼ teaspoon salt - 2 large eggs, room temperature, lightly beaten for the topping - 1 cup light brown sugar, packed - ⅔ cup dark corn syrup - 1 tablespoon dark rum - ¼ cup unsalted butter - 3 large eggs - ¼ cup heavy cream - ¼ teaspoon salt - 2 ½ cups coarsely chopped pecans instructions 1. move the oven rack to the middle position and heat the oven to 350°f. 2. line the inside bottom and sides of a 9-inch springform pan with parchment paper or aluminum foil and spray lightly with nonstick spray. 3. wrap foil around the outside bottom and set aside. 4. stir the graham cracker crumbs, ground pecans, brown sugar, and melted butter together until it resembles wet sand. 5. press the crumb mixture into the bottom and up the sides of the prepared pan, making sure it reaches at least ¾ of the way up the sides. 6. bake the crust for 10 minutes and set aside to cool. 7. reduce the oven temperature to 300°f. 8. beat the cream cheese with an electric mixer on medium to medium-high speed until smooth and creamy, about 1 minute. 9. add the sugar, sour cream, vanilla, and salt, and beat on medium speed until well combined. 10. gently stir in the eggs using a silicone spatula just until combined. 11. pour the batter into the prepared crust and spread evenly with an offset spatula. 12. bake the cheesecake for 40 minutes. 13. while the cheesecake is baking, combine the brown sugar, corn syrup, rum, and butter in a medium saucepan. 14. cook over medium heat until it reaches a boil, stirring constantly, then continue to boil for 2 minutes. 15. remove from heat and let cool while the cheesecake is baking. 16. whisk the eggs, salt, and cream together in a small bowl and set aside. 17. once the cheesecake has baked for 40 minutes, remove it from the oven. 18. slowly whisk the egg mixture with the cooled sugar syrup until well combined. 19. stir in the chopped pecans. 20. gently spoon the pecan topping over the cheesecake, adding the pecans first and then just enough syrup to fill the crust. 21. return the cheesecake to the oven and bake for another 40 to 50 minutes until the top is golden brown and crisp, covering the edges with foil if they are over-browning. 22. transfer to a wire rack and cool completely. 23. cover the cheesecake and refrigerate for at least 4 hours before serving. 24. slowly loosen the sides of the springform pan and carefully transfer the cheesecake to a serving platter. 25. freeze the cheesecake for 1 to 2 hours before slicing for neater slices. 26. run a sharp knife under hot water and carefully dry the blade, then make a cut in the cheesecake, repeating this process for each slice. 27. if you froze the cheesecake before slicing, let the slices sit at room temperature for 30 minutes before serving.

title: Perfect Pumpkin Pie

title: Pipitada (Melon Seed Drink)
text: pipitada (melon seed drink) ingredients - 1 cup sweet melon seeds - 3 cups water - 2 tablespoons caster (superfine) sugar - 1 tablespoon orange blossom water instructions 1. grind the seeds to a fine powder in a food processor a day before you want to serve. 2. put the ground seeds in cheesecloth, bring the corners together and tie securely. 3. fill a bowl with about 3 cups of water and immerse the ground seeds in their cheesecloth bag in the water. 4. leave in the fridge overnight, squeezing the cheesecloth from time to time to release the milky essence from the seeds into the water. 5. squeeze the cloth tightly to extract as much moisture as possible out of the seeds and discard the seeds. 6. add the sugar and orange blossom water to the milky liquid and refrigerate in a pitcher. 7. serve chilled.

title: Polish Cheese Cake
text: polish cheese cake source: null ingredients - 175 grams white sugar - 110 grams butter - 1 egg - 1 cup sour cream - 1 tsp vanilla extract - 375 grams flour - 1 tsp baking soda - 1 tsp baking powder - 500 grams 9% white cheese - 100 grams white sugar - 1 egg - 110 grams brown sugar - 42 grams flour - 80 grams butter - 65 grams pecans instructions 1. preheat oven to 175 degrees c. 2. grease a 9x13-inch baking dish. 3. beat 175 grams white sugar, 110 grams butter, and 1 egg in a bowl until smooth. 4. add sour cream and vanilla extract, then mix well. 5. stir in 375 grams flour, baking soda, and baking powder until mixture comes together in a sticky dough. 6. spread half the dough evenly into the prepared baking dish. 7. beat white cheese, 100 grams white sugar, and 1 egg in another bowl until smooth. 8. spoon the cheese mixture into the baking dish over the dough. 9. drop remaining half of dough by spoonfuls over the cheese mixture. 10. mix pecans, brown sugar, 42 grams flour, and 80 grams butter in a bowl until mixture resembles a coarse crumble. 11. sprinkle the crumble mixture over the dough. 12. bake in the preheated oven until a toothpick inserted into the center comes out clean, about 45 minutes.

title: Pot Roast
text: pot roast source: recipetineats.com ingredients - 2 kg / 4 lb beef chuck roast , rolled ((note 1)) - 1 tsp each salt and pepper - 2 tbsp olive oil - 1 onion ((large), cut into large dice) - 5 garlic cloves (, peeled and smashed (note 2a)) - 5 carrots (, peeled and cut into 2.5cm/1" pieces) - 3 celery stalks (, cut into 4 cm / 1.5" pieces) - 1 cup (250ml) dry red wine ((sub with beef broth)) - 3 cups (750ml) beef broth (, salt reduced) - 1/3 cup (50g) flour ((plain / all purpose) (gf - note 2b)) - 1 tsp dried rosemary - 1 1/2 tsp dried thyme - 750g / 1.5 lb potatoes (, peeled and cut into 2.5 cm / 1" pieces) instructions 1. pat beef dry with paper towels. sprinkle generously with salt and pepper all over. 2. heat oil in a skillet over high heat. brown aggressively all over - a deep dark brown crust is essential for flavour base! should take about 7 minutes. 3. transfer beef to slow cooker. 4. in the same skillet, add onion and garlic. cook for 2 minutes until onion is browned. 5. add wine, reduce by half. transfer to slow cooker. 6. mix together flour and about 1 cup of the broth. lumps is fine. pour into slow cooker. 7. add remaining broth, carrots, celery, rosemary and thyme into slow cooker. 8. cover and slow cook on low for 5 hours. text: pumpkin roll source: ohsodelicioso.com ingredients - 1 cup sugar - 3/4 cup flour - 1 teaspoon baking powder - 1 teaspoon ginger - 1 teaspoon nutmeg - 1/2 teaspoon cloves - 1/2 teaspoon salt - 2 teaspoon cinnamon - 3 eggs - 2/3 cup pumpkin - 3 cup powder sugar - 8 oz cream cheese - 1/4 cup butter - 1/2 tsp vanilla - 1-2 tablespoons milk or heavy cream instructions 1. sift flour, sugar and seasonings, and baking powder in a large bowl. add eggs and pumpkin. mix until combined. 2. pour and smooth evenly into a standard sized sheet pan lined with parchment paper. 3. bake at 375 degs for 12 mins. 4. while cake is still warm and sprinkle a light layer of powder sugar over. invert on to clean tea towel and roll up. let cool until room temperature or in refrigerator.  5. when cooled spread cream cheese filling evenly over inverted cake. gently roll cake. 6. place on large platter and sprinkle with powder sugar. 7. refrigerate and serve chilled. 8. cream together butter and cream cheese at room temp, add in vanilla and powder sugar. beat all ingredients till creamy and smooth.

title: Pumpkin Scones
text: pumpkin scones ingredients - 250g pumpkin or butternut squash, peeled and seeded - 400g plain flour - 4 tsp baking powder - ½ tsp salt - 85g butter - 80g parmesan, grated - 100ml milk - 100ml water - 2 tsp grain mustard - 1 egg, beaten, for glazing - black pepper to taste instructions 1. cut the pumpkin into large chunks and steam for 7-10 minutes until tender. 2. mix the flour, baking powder and salt in a bowl. 3. cut the butter into small chunks and rub it in with your fingertips until the mixture resembles breadcrumbs. 4. stir in the grated parmesan. 5. roughly crush the cooked pumpkin with a fork or potato masher, taking care not to reduce it to a smooth purée. 6. lightly stir in the grain mustard and a grinding of black pepper to the pumpkin. 7. add the pumpkin mixture to the flour mixture, then pour in the milk and water. 8. stir the liquids into the flour, season with black pepper and mix the ingredients carefully, taking great care not to overmix. 9. turn the dough out onto a floured board and pat it into a circle roughly 3cm thick. 10. using a 5-6cm biscuit cutter, make 12 to 14 scones and place them well apart from one another on a baking sheet. 11. brush the top of each scone with beaten egg, taking care not to let any drip down the sides. 12. bake for 12-14 minutes until they are golden. 13. remove the scones from the oven and let them rest briefly before transferring them to a cooling rack. 14. serve warm, preferably with quince jelly.

title: Ratatouille
text: ratatouille source: tasty ingredients - 2 eggplants - 6 roma tomatoes - 2 yellow squashes - 2 zucchinis - 2 tablespoons olive oil - 1 medium white onion, diced - 4 cloves garlic, minced - 1 red bell pepper, seeded and diced - 1 yellow bell pepper, seeded and diced - kosher salt, to taste - freshly ground black pepper, to taste - 28 oz crushed tomatoes (795 g) - 2 tablespoons thinly sliced fresh basil - 2 tablespoons thinly sliced fresh basil - 1 teaspoon minced garlic - 2 tablespoons finely chopped fresh parsley - 2 teaspoons fresh thyme leaves - 4 tablespoons olive oil instructions 1. preheat the oven to 375°f (190°c). 2. using a sharp knife or a mandoline, slice the eggplant, tomatoes, squash, and zucchini into approximately 1/16-inch (1-mm)-thick rounds, then set aside. 3. heat the olive oil in a 12-inch (30-cm) oven-safe pan over medium-high heat and sauté the onion, garlic, and bell peppers until soft, about 10 minutes. 4. season with salt and pepper, then add the crushed tomatoes and stir until the ingredients are fully incorporated. 5. remove from heat and add the basil, then stir once more and smooth the surface of the sauce with a spatula. 6. arrange the veggies in alternating slices (for example, eggplant, tomato, squash, zucchini) on top of the sauce, working from the outer edge to the center of the pan. 7. season the vegetables with salt and pepper. 8. in a small bowl, mix together the basil, garlic, parsley, thyme, salt, pepper, and olive oil to make the herb seasoning. 9. spoon the herb seasoning over the vegetables. 10. cover the pan with foil and bake for 40 minutes. 11. uncover and bake for another 20 minutes until the vegetables are softened. 12. serve hot as a main dish or side, or cover with foil and reheat in a 350°f (180°c) oven for 15 minutes the next day.

text: roasted sweet potatoes source: chelseasmessyapron.com ingredients - 2 pounds sweet potatoes (about 3 large, i like red garnet or jewel sweet potatoes best, peeled and cut into 1/2-inch pieces) - 2 tablespoons melted coconut oil - 3/4 teaspoon fine sea salt (use less if using table salt) - 1 tablespoon light brown sugar (firmly packed) - 2 pounds sweet potatoes (about 3 large, peeled and cut into 1/2-inch pieces) - 2 tablespoons olive oil - 3/4 teaspoon fine sea salt (use less if using table salt) - 1/4 teaspoon pepper - 1/2 teaspoon ground chili powder (see note 1) - 1/2 teaspoon paprika - 1/2 teaspoon ground cumin - 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder instructions 1. plain roasted sweet potatoes: preheat oven to 425°f. peel and cube sweet potatoes into 1/2-inch pieces. add to your largest sheet pan and add the melted coconut oil, salt, and brown sugar on top. toss to coat all the sweet potatoes, then spread out in an even layer. you don’t want any potatoes overlapping or you’ll end up with steamed potatoes instead of roasted potatoes. flip every 10–15 minutes, cooking for a total of 27–35 minutes. title: Root Beer Recipe From Scratch
text: root beer recipe from scratch ingredients - 1l water - 35g fresh ginger, unpeeled and chopped - 5g cinnamon stick - 20g dried sassafras root bark - 10g dried sarsaparilla root - 10g dried liquorice root - 7g dried cherry bark - 2 ml salt - 450g demerara brown sugar - 75g lactose (optional) - 15 ml vanilla extract - 75 ml active ginger bug (for every 2l) or 2 tsp beer yeast instructions 1. mix 1 part syrup to 3 parts water. 2. mix in active ginger bug or beer yeast. 3. pour into pressure safe bottles, filling to within 2 inches of top but no higher. 4. cap and set aside at room temperature to let ferment for 2 to 3 days. 5. check fermentation and then chill or store in refrigerator.

title: Soft Sourdough Rolls with Tangzhong
text: soft sourdough rolls with tangzhong ingredients - 145 g whole wheat flour - 160 g כפרי flour - 500 g bread flour - 35 g all-purpose flour - 530 g water - 175 g milk - 220 g levain (100% hydration) - 45 g butter - 30 g honey - 16 g salt instructions 1. combine 35 g flour and 175 g milk, then cook until thick pudding consistency and cool completely for the tangzhong. 2. mix the remaining 805 g flour, 355 g water, and all tangzhong until shaggy and rest for 1-4 hours for the autolyse. 3. add 220 g levain, 16 g salt, and 30 g honey to the autolyse and mix until combined and moderately developed. 4. add 45 g butter in pieces during the first fold, then perform 2-3 more folds every 30 minutes and bulk until approximately 40-50% rise. 5. divide dough into 15 portions of approximately 120 g each, shape into balls, and refrigerate overnight covered. 6. bake at 200°c for 15-18 minutes, optionally brushing with egg wash before baking and butter after baking.

title: Spice Squares with Molasses Whipped Cream
text: spice squares with molasses whipped cream ingredients - 2 1/2 cups sifted cake flour - 1/2 teaspoon baking soda - 2 teaspoons baking powder - 1/4 teaspoon allspice - 1/4 teaspoon mace - 1/4 teaspoon nutmeg - 1/2 teaspoon cloves - 2 teaspoons cinnamon - 1/2 cup butter or other shortening - 1 cup brown sugar, firmly packed - 2 eggs, well beaten - 1 cup sour milk or buttermilk - 2 tablespoons molasses - 1/2 cup heavy cream, whipped instructions 1. sift flour once, measure, add soda, baking powder, and spices, and sift together three times. 2. cream butter thoroughly, add sugar gradually, and cream together until light and fluffy. 3. add eggs, mixing well. 4. add flour mixture alternately with milk, a small amount at a time, beating after each addition until smooth. 5. bake in a greased 8x8x2 inch pan in a moderate oven at 350°f for 50 minutes. 6. make molasses whipped cream by folding 2 tablespoons molasses into 1/2 cup whipped cream. 7. serve cake in squares with molasses whipped cream.

title: Saffron Vanilla Donuts
text: saffron vanilla donuts source: instagram ingredients - 60g sugar - 23g cornstarch - 4 egg yolks - pinch of salt - 360g whole milk - 1 vanilla bean pod - 25g unsalted butter - 150g heavy whipping cream, cold - 0.25g saffron - 10g sugar - 30g whole milk, hot - 445g bread flour - 55g sugar - 7g salt - 185g whole milk, at 27c - 1 whole egg plus 1 yolk - 12g instant dry yeast - 70g unsalted butter, softened and cubed - frying oil - extra sugar instructions 1. whisk together egg yolks, sugar, cornstarch, and salt for the diplomat cream. 2. cut the vanilla pod in half and scrape off the beans. 3. add milk and vanilla to a pot and heat over medium heat until tiny bubbles form. 4. remove from heat and slowly pour the hot milk over the egg mixture a little at a time while whisking. 5. place a strainer over the pot and strain everything back into the pot. 6. heat over medium heat while constantly whisking until the mixture thickens. 7. remove from heat and mix in butter. 8. transfer to a bowl and cover with plastic wrap that touches the surface of the pastry cream, then refrigerate for at least an hour. 9. add saffron threads to a mortar and pestle and grind until they break down. 10. add 10g of sugar and continue grinding into a fine powder. 11. add 30g of hot milk to the saffron mixture and stir, then rest for 15 minutes. 12. add all dough ingredients except butter to the bowl of a stand mixer and knead on low for 10 minutes. 13. add butter one cube at a time to the dough. 14. knead for 10-20 minutes on low-medium until the dough passes the window-pane test. 15. proof the dough for about 90 minutes. 16. divide the dough into 15 pieces of 60g each and roll into balls. 17. arrange the dough balls on parchment paper squares and proof for 30 minutes. 18. fry the donuts at 340f/170c for 2 minutes on each side. 19. transfer fried donuts to paper towels and toss in sugar. 20. whisk 150g of cold whipping cream to soft peaks and combine with the cooled pastry cream. 21. fill the donuts with the diplomat cream and serve.
